/// A plugin that puts nothing on the context folds away, because
/// `NoContext::Install<E>` is `E`, so this is `Base` in a project whose
/// plugins all provide nothing.
type WithSessions = After<crate::plugins::sessions::Sessions, Base>;
type WithGtag = After<brocanth_gtag::Gtag, WithSessions>;
type WithAdmin = After<crate::plugins::admin::AdminSettings, WithGtag>;
type WithObservability = After<crate::plugins::observability::Observe, WithAdmin>;
type WithDb = After<crate::plugins::db::Database, WithObservability>;
type WithCache = After<crate::plugins::cache::Cache, WithDb>;
type WithJobs = After<crate::plugins::jobs::Jobs, WithCache>;
type WithAuth = After<crate::plugins::auth::Auth, WithJobs>;
type WithStorage = After<crate::plugins::storage::Files, WithAuth>;
type WithMiddlewareCsrf = After<brocanth_middleware::Csrf, WithStorage>;
type WithOpenapi = After<crate::plugins::openapi::OpenApi, WithMiddlewareCsrf>;
type WithValidation = After<crate::plugins::validation::Validation, WithOpenapi>;
type WithRealtime = After<crate::plugins::realtime::Realtime, WithValidation>;
type WithRobots = After<crate::plugins::robots::Robots, WithRealtime>;
type WithAnalytics = After<brocanth_analytics::Analytics, WithRobots>;
type WithModel = After<crate::plugins::model::Model, WithAnalytics>;
type WithMiddlewareSecurityHeaders = After<brocanth_middleware::SecurityHeaders, WithModel>;
type WithPolicy = After<crate::plugins::policy::Policies, WithMiddlewareSecurityHeaders>;
type WithMiddlewareRateLimit = After<brocanth_middleware::RateLimit, WithPolicy>;
pub type Installed = WithMiddlewareRateLimit;

type HookedGtag = Both<<brocanth_gtag::Gtag as HookSource>::Families, NoHooks>;
type HookedCsrf = Both<<brocanth_middleware::Csrf as HookSource>::Families, HookedGtag>;
type HookedAnalytics = Both<<brocanth_analytics::Analytics as HookSource>::Families, HookedCsrf>;
type HookedSecurityHeaders =
    Both<<brocanth_middleware::SecurityHeaders as HookSource>::Families, HookedAnalytics>;
type HookedRateLimit =
    Both<<brocanth_middleware::RateLimit as HookSource>::Families, HookedSecurityHeaders>;

/// Which hook families this binary installed, as a type.
///
/// One `Both` per plugin registered with `plugin_hooking`, innermost first,
/// which is exactly the record `register!` builds. A hook family nobody
/// installed costs nothing, and this type is how the compiler knows: every
/// hook entry point opens with a constant `if` on this record.
pub type Hooks = HookedRateLimit;
/// What this binary puts on the context, said once at startup.
///
/// The lines are a demonstration and they are load-bearing: the installed
/// provider set lives in the application's *type*, so an `extract` for a
/// plugin nobody registered does not compile. That is the modularity claim,
/// checked by the compiler rather than written in a README.
///
/// A handler reads the same values through `Ctx::provided`, which carries
/// the same check. This runs at startup so a misconfiguration is a failure
/// to start rather than a failure on the first request that needed it.
///
/// A macro for the reason `register!` is one: the context's type is the
/// builder's type, and neither is worth spelling.
macro_rules! announce {
    ($app:expr) => {{
        let cx = $app.context();
        let session: &crate::plugins::sessions::Session = cx.extract();
        let cookie = &session.cookie;
        crate::plugins::say!(info, "session cookie: {cookie}"; %cookie);
        let db: &brocanth_db::Db = cx.extract();
        let connections = db.pool().size();
        crate::plugins::say!(info, "db: {connections} connection(s) open"; connections);
        let auth: &crate::plugins::auth::Services = cx.extract();
        let cookie = &auth.sessions().config().cookie_name;
        let providers = auth.providers().len();
        crate::plugins::say!(
            info,
            "auth: session cookie {cookie}, {providers} provider(s)";
            %cookie,
            providers
        );
        let files: &plugins::storage::FileStore = cx.extract();
        let ttl = files.tokens.ttl();
        crate::plugins::say!(info, "storage: ready, download links last {ttl}s"; ttl);
        let checks: &brocanth_schema::Validation = cx.extract();
        let style = checks.report_style();
        crate::plugins::say!(info, "validation: reports as {style:?}"; ?style);
        let realtime: &crate::plugins::realtime::Broadcast = cx.extract();
        let max_clients = realtime.broker.config().max_clients;
        crate::plugins::say!(info, "realtime: up to {max_clients} clients"; max_clients);
        let rules: &crate::plugins::policy::Rules = cx.extract();
        let dialect = &rules.dialect;
        crate::plugins::say!(info, "policy: compiling for {dialect:?}"; ?dialect);
    }};
}
pub(crate) use announce;

/// A line about the application itself: startup, the listener, the stop.
///
/// A `tracing` event, because `observability-logs` is installed: the line is
/// JSON in production and text elsewhere, on stdout, like the request lines.
/// The fields after `;` are the event's fields, in `tracing`'s shorthand
/// (`addr`, `%addr`, `?addr`), and name variables already in scope.
///
/// ```ignore
/// plugins::say!(info, "listening on http://{bound}"; %bound);
/// ```
///
/// Before the observability plugin installs its subscriber (a config file
/// that does not parse, a plugin that fails before it) and with
/// `install_subscriber = false`, an event would go nowhere. Then this is a
/// line on stderr, as it is without `observability-logs`.
macro_rules! say {
    ($level:ident, $message:literal $(; $($field:tt)+)?) => {
        if brocanth_observe::tracing::dispatcher::has_been_set() {
            brocanth_observe::tracing::$level!($($($field)+,)? $message)
        } else {
            eprintln!("{}: {}", crate::app::APP, format_args!($message))
        }
    };
}
pub(crate) use say;

/// One middleware layer, as the stack stores it.
///
/// A name rather than the type written out: clippy calls the bare
/// form a very complex type, and it is also the type `src/app.rs`
/// would have to spell to hold one.
///
/// A layer may wait, so it returns a future. The lifetime is named
/// because the future borrows both the context and the rest of the
/// chain; see `sessions::layer` for the shape of one.
pub type Layer = for<'a> fn(&'a mut Ctx, AsyncNext<'a, Ctx, Response>) -> BoxFuture<'a, Response>;

/// The function behind a middleware name the application mounted.
///
/// Mounting is `src/app.rs`'s decision and stays there: the pattern is a
/// decision and the decision is the application's. Which function answers
/// to `"session"` is not a decision, so it is here, where adding a
/// plugin can write it.
pub fn layer(name: &str) -> Option<Layer> {
    match name {
        "session" => Some(sessions::layer),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// One declared setting, by the key it sets.
pub struct Setting {
    /// The key, as `config/<env>.toml` spells it. It is also the flag's name,
    /// unless `src/flags.rs` renames it.
    pub path: &'static str,
    /// The line `--help` prints.
    pub help: &'static str,
    /// Whether a flag may set it. A secret has none: every user on the host
    /// can read a process's arguments.
    pub flag: bool,
    /// A value that means `None` as well as an empty one does.
    pub none_as: Option<&'static str>,
    /// Whether a flag's value stays a string whatever it looks like.
    pub text: bool,
}

/// One value this run was given, above the defaults.
pub struct Given {
    /// What it sets.
    pub setting: &'static Setting,
    /// Where it came from, as typed: `--cookie`, or `$MY_APP_SESSIONS__COOKIE`.
    pub from: String,
    /// The value, as typed. Empty is `None` for an `Option` setting.
    pub value: String,
}

/// The name each flag answers to after `src/flags.rs`, whether the flags are
/// read or not.
///
/// A rename of a key no flag sets, a name that is not spelled as a flag, and
/// two flags under one name each stop the binary: each would otherwise be a
/// flag that does nothing, or does something else.
fn names() -> Result<Vec<(&'static Setting, &'static str)>, String> {
    let flags = || SETTINGS.iter().filter(|setting| setting.flag);
    for (path, _) in crate::flags::RENAMES {
        if !flags().any(|setting| setting.path == *path) {
            let known: Vec<&str> = flags().map(|setting| setting.path).collect();
            return Err(format!(
                "src/flags.rs renames `{path}`, and no flag sets it\nhelp: the flags are {}",
                known.join(", ")
            ));
        }
    }
    let mut names: Vec<(&'static Setting, &'static str)> = Vec::new();
    for setting in flags() {
        let name = crate::flags::RENAMES
            .iter()
            .find(|(path, _)| *path == setting.path)
            .map_or(setting.path, |(_, name)| *name);
        if name.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let spelled = name
            .chars()
            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c.is_ascii_digit() || "._-".contains(c));
        let taken = ["help", "version", "settings"].contains(&name);
        if !spelled || name.starts_with(['-', '.', '_']) || taken {
            return Err(format!(
                "src/flags.rs names a flag `{name}`\nhelp: a flag is lower case, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or a digit, and is not `help`, `version` or `settings`"
            ));
        }
        if let Some((other, _)) = names.iter().find(|(_, taken)| *taken == name) {
            return Err(format!(
                "`--{name}` would set both `{}` and `{}`\nhelp: rename one of them in src/flags.rs",
                other.path, setting.path
            ));
        }
        names.push((setting, name));
    }
    Ok(names)
}

/// The flags this run reads: none unless `src/flags.rs` turns them on,
/// because with a config file the file is the source.
pub fn flag_names() -> Result<Vec<(&'static Setting, &'static str)>, String> {
    if !crate::flags::WITH_CONFIG {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    }
    names()
}

/// A flag given while the flags are off, refused by name with what to do
/// instead. Silently ignoring it would run with a value nobody chose.
pub fn refuse_off_flags() -> Result<(), String> {
    if crate::flags::WITH_CONFIG {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let names = names()?;
    for arg in std::env::args_os().skip(1) {
        let arg = arg.to_string_lossy();
        if arg == "--" {
            break;
        }
        let Some(written) = arg.strip_prefix("--") else {
            continue;
        };
        let name = written.split_once('=').map_or(written, |(name, _)| name);
        if let Some((setting, _)) = names.iter().find(|(_, known)| *known == name) {
            let (section, key) = setting.path.rsplit_once('.').unwrap_or(("", setting.path));
            return Err(format!(
                "`--{name}` is off: this project reads its settings from config/<env>.toml\nhelp: set WITH_CONFIG = true in src/flags.rs, or set `{key}` under [{section}] in config/<env>.toml"
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The flags this run was given, in the order typed. The environment is not
/// here: `brocanth-config` reads it, under the file and over the flags.
///
/// `--name=VALUE` and `--name VALUE`. Every other argument is left alone: it
/// is a command's, and the command line's own parser has already refused what
/// nobody declared.
pub fn given() -> Result<Vec<Given>, String> {
    let mut given = Vec::new();
    let names = flag_names()?;
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args_os()
        .skip(1)
        .map(|arg| arg.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        .collect();
    let mut rest = args.iter();
    while let Some(arg) = rest.next() {
        if arg == "--" {
            break;
        }
        let Some(written) = arg.strip_prefix("--") else {
            continue;
        };
        let (name, inline) = match written.split_once('=') {
            Some((name, value)) => (name, Some(value.to_string())),
            None => (written, None),
        };
        let Some((setting, name)) = names.iter().copied().find(|(_, known)| *known == name) else {
            continue;
        };
        let value = match inline {
            Some(value) => value,
            None => rest
                .next()
                .cloned()
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("--{name} needs a value\nhelp: write --{name}=VALUE"))?,
        };
        given.push(Given {
            setting,
            from: format!("--{name}"),
            value,
        });
    }
    Ok(given)
}

/// The configuration this run reads: the files, the environment, and the
/// flags on top once `src/flags.rs` turns them on.
pub fn config() -> Result<brocanth_config::Config, String> {
    refuse_off_flags()?;
    let mut loader = brocanth_config::Loader::new(crate::app::APP);
    for setting in SETTINGS {
        if let Some(alias) = setting.none_as {
            loader = loader.none_as(setting.path, alias);
        }
    }
    for given in given()? {
        let flag = given.from.trim_start_matches('-');
        loader = loader.flag(given.setting.path, flag, &given.value, given.setting.text);
    }
    loader.load().map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

/// The flags, as arguments every command takes.
///
/// A name a command already takes is refused here: `clap` panics on it in a
/// debug build and lets one of the two win in a release one.
pub fn flag_args(
    command: brocanth_command::clap::Command,
) -> brocanth_command::anyhow::Result<brocanth_command::clap::Command> {
    use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap};

    refuse_off_flags().map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?;
    let mut command = command;
    for (setting, name) in flag_names().map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)? {
        let taken = command
            .get_subcommands()
            .flat_map(|sub| sub.get_arguments())
            .any(|arg| arg.get_long() == Some(name));
        if taken {
            anyhow::bail!(
                "`--{name}` sets `{}` and is also an argument of a command\nhelp: rename it in src/flags.rs",
                setting.path
            );
        }
        command = command.arg(
            clap::Arg::new(name)
                .long(name)
                .value_name("VALUE")
                .help(setting.help)
                .global(true)
                .action(clap::ArgAction::Append),
        );
    }
    Ok(command)
}

/// Every settings layer on its own, lowest first, then the merged values.
/// A secret is masked in every layer.
pub fn settings_report() -> Result<String, String> {
    let config = config()?;
    let mut layers = config.layers().defaults(defaults());
    for setting in SETTINGS.iter().filter(|setting| !setting.flag) {
        layers = layers.secret(setting.path);
    }
    Ok(layers.to_string())
}

/// `[server]`: the settings the framework reads itself. It declares them as
/// a module declares its own, so each has a flag, a variable and a line in
/// the settings report.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ServerSettings {
    /// Seconds a stop waits for open requests, then for the plugins.
    pub shutdown_grace_secs: u64,
}

impl Default for ServerSettings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            shutdown_grace_secs: crate::app::SHUTDOWN_GRACE.as_secs(),
        }
    }
}

/// `[server] shutdown_grace_secs` from the files, the environment and the
/// flags, or [`SHUTDOWN_GRACE`](crate::app::SHUTDOWN_GRACE) when none sets it.
pub fn shutdown_grace() -> Result<std::time::Duration, String> {
    let config = config()?;
    let Some(value) = config
        .raw_section("server")
        .and_then(|server| server.get("shutdown_grace_secs"))
    else {
        return Ok(crate::app::SHUTDOWN_GRACE);
    };
    // An integer in a file, a flag or a variable; a string when a layer
    // could not type it.
    value
        .as_integer()
        .and_then(|secs| u64::try_from(secs).ok())
        .or_else(|| value.as_str().and_then(|secs| secs.trim().parse().ok()))
        .map(std::time::Duration::from_secs)
        .ok_or_else(|| {
            format!(
                "`[server] shutdown_grace_secs` is {}, and it must be a whole number of seconds\nhelp: set it to a whole number of seconds, such as 25",
                value.display()
            )
        })
}

/// What the server is handed for one request.
pub type Answer = brocanth::plugin_routes::BoxFuture<'static, brocanth_server::Response>;

/// What `serve` answers a request with: `next`, observed. The `observe`
/// plugin answers `/up`, `/readyz` and `/metrics` itself, and logs and
/// counts every other request by its route template.
pub fn wrap<F, Fut>(
    app: &std::sync::Arc<crate::app::App>,
    next: F,
) -> impl Fn(brocanth_server::Request) -> Answer + Send + Sync + 'static
where
    F: Fn(brocanth_server::Request) -> Fut + Send + Sync + 'static,
    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = brocanth_server::Response> + Send + 'static,
{
    let routes = std::sync::Arc::clone(app);
    observer(app).wrap_routed(next, move |request| {
        routes
            .router
            .at(&request.path)
            .map(|found| found.template().to_string())
    })
}

/// The probes and `/metrics` on a second listener, when
/// `[observability] metrics_bind` names one.
pub async fn side_listeners(app: &crate::app::App) -> Result<(), String> {
    let observer = observer(app);
    let Some(bind) = observer.config().metrics_bind.clone() else {
        return Ok(());
    };
    let server = brocanth_server::Server::bind(&bind)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    tokio::spawn(async move {
        let _ = observer.serve_admin(server).await;
    });
    Ok(())
}

/// The first half of a stop. `/readyz` fails at once, so a load balancer
/// stops sending requests; the listener closes `[observability] drain_delay_secs`
/// later.
pub async fn stop_accepting(app: &crate::app::App, stopper: brocanth_server::Stopper) {
    observer(app).drain_then_stop(stopper).await;
}

/// The `Observer` the `observability` plugin published.
fn observer(app: &crate::app::App) -> brocanth_observe::Observer {
    app.core
        .services()
        .get::<brocanth_observe::Observer>()
        .cloned()
        .expect("`observability` is registered in `register!`")
}

// brocanth-digest: 4119a3f3ad59191c
===== src/flags.rs =====
//! The command-line flags of this binary, and the one place to rename them.
//!
//! A module declares each of its settings once. From that the binary takes a
//! flag, `--<module>.<key>=VALUE`, an environment variable,
//! `$<APP>_<MODULE>__<KEY>`, and, with the `config` module, a key in
//! `config/<env>.toml`. `brocanth add` rewrites the list in
//! `src/plugins/mod.rs`. This file is yours: it is written when it is missing
//! and never again.

/// Whether a project with a config file reads the flags too.
///
/// Off: with the `config` module, the file and the environment are the
/// sources, and a flag is refused with a pointer to this line. On: a flag
/// outranks both, for one run. Without the `config` module the flags are
/// always read, and this is not.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub const WITH_CONFIG: bool = false;

/// Flags under another name: the key as the module declares it, and the flag
/// this binary answers to instead, without `--`. An empty name hides the
/// flag.
///
/// ```text
/// ("sessions.cookie", "cookie"),
/// ("storage.root", ""),
/// ```
pub const RENAMES: &[(&str, &str)] = &[];

===== src/commands/serve.rs =====
//! `serve` -- the one command the scaffold wrote.
//!
//! It is ordinary project code: rename it, give it more flags, or delete it.
//! The framework does not own this command line.

use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap, cmd, Command, Context};

/// Serve the application over HTTP.
#[cmd]
#[derive(clap::Args)]
pub struct Serve {
    /// Address to bind.
    #[arg(long, default_value_t = crate::app::default_addr())]
    pub addr: String,
}

impl Command for Serve {
    fn run(self, _ctx: &mut Context) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        crate::app::serve(&self.addr).map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)
    }
}
===== src/commands/settings.rs =====
//! `settings` -- every settings layer on its own, then the merged values.
//!
//! Ordinary project code, like `serve`: rename it or delete it, and delete
//! its line in `src/commands/mod.rs`.

use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap, cmd, Command, Context};

/// Show each settings layer, lowest precedence first, then the merged values.
#[cmd]
#[derive(clap::Args)]
pub struct Settings {}

impl Command for Settings {
    fn run(self, _ctx: &mut Context) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        print!(
            "{}",
            crate::plugins::settings_report().map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?
        );
        Ok(())
    }
}

===== .github/workflows/ci.yml =====
# Every push and every pull request: formatting, lints, tests.
#
# The toolchain is the one `rust-toolchain.toml` pins. A dependency on a path
# outside this repository (`brocanth create --brocanth-path`) is not in the
# checkout, and the build fails; depend on git instead.
name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        env:
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
        ports: ["5432:5432"]
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready --health-interval 5s --health-timeout 5s --health-retries 10
    env:
      # The tests that need Postgres read this; without it they skip.
      BROCANTH_TEST_DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # Reads rust-toolchain.toml, and caches the target directory.
      - uses: actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain@v1
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      - run: cargo fmt --all --check
      - run: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - run: cargo test

  image:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      # Builds the image and pushes nothing. Add a registry login and
      # `push: true` when there is somewhere to push to.
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          push: false
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
===== Dockerfile =====
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# The image of My Blog.
#
#   docker build -t my-blog .
#   docker run --rm -p 3000:3000 my-blog
#
# Three stages. `planner` reduces the manifests to a recipe. `builder` builds
# the dependencies from the recipe, in a layer that stays cached until
# Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock changes, and then builds the application. The
# runtime holds the binary, the config directory and nothing else.
#
# Dependencies on a path outside this directory (`brocanth create
# --brocanth-path`) are not in the build context, and the build fails. Build
# from git dependencies, or add the checkout to the context.

ARG RUST_VERSION=1.98

FROM rust:${RUST_VERSION}-slim-bookworm AS chef
RUN cargo install cargo-chef --locked
WORKDIR /app

FROM chef AS planner
COPY . .
RUN cargo chef prepare --recipe-path recipe.json

FROM chef AS builder
COPY --from=planner /app/recipe.json recipe.json
RUN cargo chef cook --release --recipe-path recipe.json
COPY . .
RUN cargo build --release --bin my-blog \
 && mkdir -p config

FROM debian:bookworm-slim AS runtime
# ca-certificates for TLS to a database or an API; curl for HEALTHCHECK.
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN useradd --system --uid 10001 --home-dir /app --shell /usr/sbin/nologin app
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=builder /app/target/release/my-blog /app/my-blog
COPY --from=builder /app/config /app/config
USER 10001

# Every interface, inside the container. `$MY_BLOG_ENV` picks
# config/production.toml, and a variable such as `$MY_BLOG_DB__URL`
# overrides one key of it.
ENV MY_BLOG_ADDR=0.0.0.0:3000 \
    MY_BLOG_ENV=production
EXPOSE 3000

# `/up` is the liveness probe of `observability-health`. Any HTTP answer
# passes, so a project without it passes with a 404: the process answers.
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=3s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
  CMD curl -sS -o /dev/null --max-time 2 http://127.0.0.1:3000/up || exit 1

# `serve` drains on SIGTERM for `[server] shutdown_grace_secs` (25 by
# default). Give `docker stop` more than that: `docker stop -t 30`.
STOPSIGNAL SIGTERM
CMD ["/app/my-blog", "serve"]
===== assets/css/_tailwind.css =====
/* The input of the CSS build. Never published.
 *
 * The leading underscore marks an input: a file that is bundled into another
 * and that `assets!` must not publish on its own. The build reads this file
 * and writes assets/css/site.css, which is the one that ships:
 *
 *     brocanth css          # once, minified
 *     brocanth css -W       # again on each change
 */

@import "tailwindcss";

/* Where the class names are.
 *
 * Tailwind resolves each path against this stylesheet and keeps its automatic
 * detection on as well. These are explicit for two reasons: `.rsx` is not an
 * extension Tailwind knows, and an explicit glob states the contract.
 */

/* The templates. A .rsx file is Rust with an HTML-shaped body. */
@source "../../src/pages/**/*.rsx";

/* Plain Rust holds class names too -- a helper that builds a class string,
 * or a handler choosing one. */
@source "../../src/**/*.rs";
===== assets/css/site.css =====
/* Written by `brocanth create` so the first build works.
   `brocanth css` replaces it with the real one. */
===== deploy/kubernetes.yaml =====
# A minimal deployment of this image. Change the image, the replica count
# and the secrets; keep the probes and the timings in step.
#
# The stop, in order:
#   1. SIGTERM. `/readyz` answers 503 at once, so the Service stops routing
#      here. The listener stays open for `drain_delay_secs` (5 below), while
#      the endpoint change reaches every node.
#   2. The listener closes. Open requests have what is left of
#      `shutdown_grace_secs` (25) to finish, then the plugins stop.
#   3. terminationGracePeriodSeconds (30) is the hard limit: SIGKILL. It is
#      above the 25, so a clean drain never meets it.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-blog
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-blog
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-blog
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10001
      containers:
        - name: my-blog
          image: my-blog:latest
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 3000
          env:
            - name: MY_BLOG_SERVER__SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECS
              value: "25"
            - name: MY_BLOG_OBSERVABILITY__DRAIN_DELAY_SECS
              value: "5"
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /up
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 10
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /readyz
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 2
            failureThreshold: 1
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: my-blog
spec:
  selector:
    app: my-blog
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: http
===== migrations/mod.rs =====
//! Written by `brocanth`. Do not edit -- the `migrate` tool rewrites this file.
//! A migration is a file beside this one; `migrate make` and `migrate sync` list it here.
//!
//! The migrations in this directory, oldest first.
//!
//! A file name starts with its UTC time, so the order of the names is the
//! order the migrations were written. `src/commands/migrate.rs` applies this
//! list, and `src/main.rs` reaches this file through `#[path]`.

use brocanth_model::sea_orm_migration::prelude::*;

/// Every migration this binary applies, oldest first.
pub struct Migrator;

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl MigratorTrait for Migrator {
    fn migrations() -> Vec<Box<dyn MigrationTrait>> {
        vec![]
    }
}

//# sourceMappingURL=dpswap.min.js.map
===== src/assets.rs =====
//! Every static file this binary serves.
//!
//! Two directories, two rules. `assets/` is **fingerprinted** -- `site.css`
//! is published at `/css/site.<hash>.css`, so it can be cached forever and a
//! new build invalidates it by having a different name. `public/` is served
//! **verbatim**, because `robots.txt`, `favicon.ico` and anything linked to
//! from outside must keep the name they were given.
//!
//! Write a reference with `assets::url`, never by hand:
//!
//! ```ignore
//! <link rel="stylesheet" href={assets::url("css/site.css")}>
//! ```
//!
//! A name nothing publishes panics there rather than 404ing in a browser.
//!
//! Embedded, like the templates and the route table, so `serve` works from
//! any directory and nothing can go missing after the build passed. A file
//! added where there was none needs `touch src/assets.rs`, because nothing
//! referenced it yet.

brocanth_assets::assets!("assets", "public");
===== src/bin/migrate.rs =====
//! The `migrate` tool: write migrations from the models in `src/models/`.
//!
//! ```text
//! cargo run --bin migrate -- ids              # an id on each model and field
//! cargo run --bin migrate -- make add_posts   # a migration for what changed
//! cargo run --bin migrate -- sync             # list every file in migrations/mod.rs
//! ```
//!
//! A development tool, and a binary of its own: it parses Rust source, and
//! the server has no reason to link a parser. It applies nothing. Apply
//! with the application's own `migrate up`.

fn main() -> std::process::ExitCode {
    brocanth_migrate::tool::main()
}
===== src/commands/admin.rs =====
//! `admin eject` and `admin diff` -- shipped admin screens, copied into
//! this project and compared with the shipped ones.
//!
//! The work is the `brocanth` CLI's. This command runs
//! `brocanth admin eject <screen> [--model <key>]` or
//! `brocanth admin diff [<screen>] [--model <key>]` in the project root and
//! exits with its status, so `cargo run -- admin eject list` and
//! `brocanth admin eject list` do the same thing. The application does not
//! link the code that writes source.
//!
//! This file is yours. See `docs/admin-customization.md`, level 8.

use std::ffi::OsStr;
use std::path::Path;
use std::process;

use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap, cmd, Command, Context};

/// Work on the admin: `eject` copies a shipped screen into this project,
/// `diff` compares the copies with the shipped screens.
#[cmd]
#[derive(clap::Args)]
pub struct Admin {
    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub action: Action,
}

#[derive(clap::Subcommand)]
pub enum Action {
    /// Copy a shipped screen into this project and install it over the
    /// default. `brocanth admin eject --help` lists the screens.
    Eject {
        /// The screen to copy, such as `list` or `layout`.
        screen: String,
        /// Install the copy for this model only. list, detail, form and
        /// delete take one.
        #[arg(long, value_name = "KEY")]
        model: Option<String>,
    },
    /// Compare ejected screens with the shipped ones of the installed
    /// brocanth-admin. Run it after an upgrade.
    Diff {
        /// The screen to compare. Without one, every ejected copy.
        screen: Option<String>,
        /// Compare the copy for this model only.
        #[arg(long, value_name = "KEY", requires = "screen")]
        model: Option<String>,
    },
}

impl Command for Admin {
    fn run(self, ctx: &mut Context) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let status = brocanth(OsStr::new("brocanth"), ctx.root(), &self.action.args())?;
        if !status.success() {
            // `brocanth` printed the error and its help line.
            process::exit(status.code().unwrap_or(1));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Action {
    /// The `brocanth` arguments this action stands for.
    fn args(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        match self {
            Action::Eject { screen, model } => {
                let mut args = vec!["admin".to_string(), "eject".to_string(), screen.clone()];
                if let Some(model) = model {
                    args.extend(["--model".to_string(), model.clone()]);
                }
                args
            }
            Action::Diff { screen, model } => {
                let mut args = vec!["admin".to_string(), "diff".to_string()];
                args.extend(screen.clone());
                if let Some(model) = model {
                    args.extend(["--model".to_string(), model.clone()]);
                }
                args
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Runs `program` with `args` in `root`. A program that is not installed
/// is an error that says how to install it.
fn brocanth(program: &OsStr, root: &Path, args: &[String]) -> anyhow::Result<process::ExitStatus> {
    let name = program.to_string_lossy();
    process::Command::new(program)
        .args(args)
        .current_dir(root)
        .status()
        .map_err(|e| match e.kind() {
            std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => anyhow::anyhow!(
                "`{name}` is not installed or not on PATH\n\
                 help: install the brocanth CLI: `cargo install --git \
                 https://github.com/DHHwasRight/brocanth brocanth-cli`, or \
                 `cargo install --path crates/brocanth-cli` in a brocanth checkout"
            ),
            _ => anyhow::anyhow!("could not run `{name}`: {e}"),
        })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn eject_passes_the_screen_and_the_model_through() {
        let action = Action::Eject {
            screen: "list".to_string(),
            model: Some("post".to_string()),
        };
        assert_eq!(action.args(), ["admin", "eject", "list", "--model", "post"]);
        let action = Action::Eject {
            screen: "layout".to_string(),
            model: None,
        };
        assert_eq!(action.args(), ["admin", "eject", "layout"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn diff_passes_the_screen_and_the_model_through() {
        let action = Action::Diff {
            screen: Some("list".to_string()),
            model: Some("post".to_string()),
        };
        assert_eq!(action.args(), ["admin", "diff", "list", "--model", "post"]);
        let action = Action::Diff {
            screen: None,
            model: None,
        };
        assert_eq!(action.args(), ["admin", "diff"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_missing_cli_says_how_to_install_it() {
        let error = brocanth(
            OsStr::new("brocanth-that-is-not-installed"),
            Path::new("."),
            &[],
        )
        .expect_err("no such program");
        let message = error.to_string();
        assert!(
            message.contains("not installed or not on PATH"),
            "{message}"
        );
        assert!(
            message.contains("help: install the brocanth CLI"),
            "{message}"
        );
    }
}
===== src/commands/api.rs =====
//! This application, from the outside.
//!
//! `cargo run -- api --help` lists every operation, because the list is
//! `crate::pages::described()` -- the same table the OpenAPI document is
//! built from, read off the handler signatures while this crate compiled.
//! There is nothing to regenerate: add a page and the client grows a
//! subcommand.
//!
//! ```text
//! $ cargo run -- api signup-post --handle ada-lovelace --age 36
//! {"id":"0191a3f0-0000-7000-8000-000000000000","handle":"ada-lovelace"}
//! ```
//!
//! The flags come from the request body's own schema, and their help text
//! is the sentence each field carries. Nothing here re-checks a rule: the
//! server is the authority, and a client that validated too would be a
//! second opinion that can disagree with it.

use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap, cmd, Command, Context};

/// Call this application's own API.
#[cmd]
#[derive(clap::Args)]
pub struct Api {
    /// The operation and its flags. `api --help` lists them.
    #[arg(trailing_var_arg = true, allow_hyphen_values = true, num_args = 0..)]
    pub rest: Vec<String>,
}

impl Command for Api {
    fn run(self, _ctx: &mut Context) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let routes = crate::pages::described();
        let wire = brocanth_client::Reqwest::new().map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?;

        let mut argv: Vec<std::ffi::OsString> = vec!["api".into()];
        argv.extend(self.rest.into_iter().map(std::ffi::OsString::from));

        let answered =
            brocanth_client::run("api", &routes, &wire, argv).map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?;

        println!("{}", answered.body);
        // The status is the exit code, so `api ... && something` means what
        // it looks like in a shell. The body is still printed, because a
        // 422 from this framework carries every fault and that is the part
        // worth reading.
        if !answered.ok() {
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
===== src/commands/check.rs =====
//! `check` -- what is wrong before it is live.
//!
//! Reads the configuration of one environment the way the application does,
//! `brocanth.toml`, and `src/` as text. Nothing is built and nothing
//! connects, so it runs in CI. `--deploy` adds the production checks; the
//! list is in `brocanth_config::check`. `brocanth check` runs this command
//! after the checks only the CLI can make.
//!
//! Ordinary project code, like `serve`: rename it or delete it, and delete
//! its line in `src/commands/mod.rs`.

use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap, cmd, Command, Context};
use brocanth_config::check::{self, Options};

/// Check the configuration and the source; --deploy adds the production checks.
#[cmd]
#[derive(clap::Args)]
pub struct Check {
    /// Add the production checks: secrets, cookies, CSRF, the admin, the database
    #[arg(long)]
    deploy: bool,
    /// The environment to load [default: production with --deploy, else $<APP>_ENV or development]
    #[arg(long, short, value_name = "ENV")]
    env: Option<String>,
    /// Silence one finding by its id, such as deploy/hsts. Repeat for more
    #[arg(long, value_name = "ID")]
    allow: Vec<String>,
    /// Exit 1 on a warning too
    #[arg(long)]
    strict: bool,
}

impl Command for Check {
    fn run(self, ctx: &mut Context) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let options = Options {
            deploy: self.deploy,
            env: self.env,
            allow: self.allow,
        };
        let report = check::run(crate::app::APP, ctx.root(), &options)?;
        eprint!("{report}");
        if report.failed(self.strict) {
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
===== src/commands/css.rs =====
//! `css` -- build assets/css/site.css from assets/css/_tailwind.css.
//!
//!     brocanth css          once, minified
//!     brocanth css -W       again on each change
//!
//! Ordinary project code, like `serve`: rename it, give it more flags, or
//! delete it. It is here rather than in a shell script because this project
//! already has a command line, and a second way to run things is a second
//! thing to keep in step.
//!
//! The Tailwind CLI comes out of `node_modules` and there is no fallback to
//! `npx`. A fallback downloads some other version and hides the one fact
//! worth knowing, which is that nobody ran `npm install`.

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::Command as Child;

use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap, cmd, Command, Context};

/// Build the stylesheet from the Tailwind input.
#[cmd]
#[derive(clap::Args)]
pub struct Css {
    /// Rebuild on each change instead of once.
    #[arg(short = 'W', long)]
    pub watch: bool,
}

const INPUT: &str = "assets/css/_tailwind.css";
const OUTPUT: &str = "assets/css/site.css";
const CLI: &str = "node_modules/.bin/tailwindcss";

impl Command for Css {
    fn run(self, ctx: &mut Context) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        // The project root and not the working directory: `brocanth css`
        // runs from wherever you happen to be, and every path below is
        // written relative to the project.
        let root = ctx.root();
        let cli = root.join(CLI);
        if !cli.is_file() {
            anyhow::bail!(
                "the Tailwind CLI is absent at {}\n       run `npm install` in {} first",
                cli.display(),
                root.display()
            );
        }

        let mut child = Child::new(&cli);
        child
            .current_dir(root)
            .args(["--input", INPUT, "--output", OUTPUT]);
        if self.watch {
            child.arg("--watch");
        } else {
            child.arg("--minify");
        }

        let status = child.status()?;
        if !status.success() {
            // No message beyond this: the CLI has already written its own
            // on the stderr this process inherited.
            anyhow::bail!("the Tailwind CLI failed");
        }

        // `--watch` only ever returns when it was interrupted, and the
        // output it leaves behind is whatever the last change produced.
        // Checking it, or touching the module below, would both be about a
        // build that is over.
        if self.watch {
            return Ok(());
        }

        let written = root.join(OUTPUT);
        let bytes = std::fs::metadata(&written)?.len();
        if bytes == 0 {
            anyhow::bail!("the build wrote no CSS to {}", written.display());
        }

        touch(&root.join("src/assets.rs"))?;
        println!("built {OUTPUT} ({bytes} bytes)");
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Make cargo notice a stylesheet it has already compiled in.
///
/// The CSS is embedded at compile time, so a new one is a new binary, and
/// nothing rebuilds until the module that embeds it looks newer than the
/// artefact. Rewriting its own bytes is the portable way to say so: there is
/// no `utimes` in `std`, and a dependency for one call is not worth it.
fn touch(path: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let same = std::fs::read(path)?;
    std::fs::write(path, same)?;
    Ok(())
}
===== src/commands/dbshell.rs =====
//! `dbshell` -- the database's own client, on this application's database.
//!
//! Reads `[db] url` the way the server does and replaces itself with `psql`
//! or `sqlite3` on it. `--print` shows the command line; a password goes in
//! `PGPASSWORD` and never on it. See `brocanth_db::shell`.
//!
//! Ordinary project code, like `serve`: rename it or delete it, and delete
//! its line in `src/commands/mod.rs`.

use std::ffi::OsString;

use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap, cmd, Command, Context};

/// Open psql or sqlite3 on the database in `[db] url`
#[cmd]
#[derive(clap::Args)]
pub struct Dbshell {
    /// The environment whose `[db] url` to open [default: $<APP>_ENV, or development]
    #[arg(long, short, value_name = "ENV")]
    env: Option<String>,
    /// Print the command line instead of running it. The password is not printed
    #[arg(long)]
    print: bool,
    /// Passed to psql or sqlite3 unchanged, after `--`
    #[arg(last = true, value_name = "CLIENT ARGS")]
    rest: Vec<OsString>,
}

impl Command for Dbshell {
    fn run(self, ctx: &mut Context) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let url = url(self.env.as_deref(), ctx.root())?;
        brocanth_db::shell::run(&url, ctx.root(), self.print, &self.rest)?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// `[db] url`, through the loader the server uses, so the files,
/// `$<APP>_ENV` and `$<APP>_DB__URL` agree with what the server sees.
fn url(env: Option<&str>, root: &std::path::Path) -> anyhow::Result<String> {
    let mut loader = brocanth_config::Loader::new(crate::app::APP).cwd(root);
    if let Some(env) = env {
        loader = loader.env(env);
    }
    Ok(loader
        .load()?
        .section::<crate::plugins::db::Settings>("db")?
        .url)
}
===== src/commands/migrate.rs =====
//! `migrate` -- apply the migrations in `migrations/` to `[db] url`.
//!
//! `up`, `down [N]` and `status` run in this binary, because the
//! migrations are compiled into it. Where there is no `brocanth` -- a
//! container, a release job -- run the binary itself: `<binary> migrate up`.
//! `brocanth migrate up` hands over to this command too.
//!
//! `ids`, `make <NAME>` and `sync` write source, so they run the `migrate`
//! tool, `src/bin/migrate.rs`, through cargo. The tool is a binary of its
//! own so this one links no Rust parser.

use std::collections::BTreeSet;

use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap, cmd, Command, Context};
use brocanth_db::{Db, DbConfig};
use brocanth_model::sea_orm_migration::{MigrationStatus, MigratorTrait};
use brocanth_model::Orm;

use crate::migrations::Migrator;

/// Apply, roll back or list the migrations in migrations/
#[cmd]
#[derive(clap::Args)]
pub struct Migrate {
    #[command(subcommand)]
    action: Action,
}

#[derive(clap::Subcommand)]
enum Action {
    /// Apply each pending migration, oldest first
    Up,
    /// Roll back the newest N applied migrations
    Down {
        /// How many migrations to roll back
        #[arg(value_name = "N", default_value_t = 1)]
        n: u32,
    },
    /// List each migration as applied or pending
    Status,
    /// Write an id on each model and field in src/models that has none
    Ids,
    /// Write a migration for what changed in src/models since the last one
    Make {
        /// The name of the migration, in snake case: add_posts, rename_title
        #[arg(value_name = "NAME")]
        name: String,
        /// Write the snapshot and no migration
        #[arg(long)]
        snapshot_only: bool,
    },
    /// List every migrations/m*.rs file in migrations/mod.rs
    Sync,
}

impl Command for Migrate {
    fn run(self, ctx: &mut Context) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        // The config files resolve from the project root, wherever the
        // command started.
        std::env::set_current_dir(ctx.root())?;
        match self.action {
            Action::Ids => tool(&["ids"]),
            Action::Sync => tool(&["sync"]),
            Action::Make {
                name,
                snapshot_only,
            } => {
                let mut args = vec!["make", name.as_str()];
                if snapshot_only {
                    args.push("--snapshot-only");
                }
                tool(&args)
            }
            Action::Up => apply(Apply::Up),
            Action::Down { n } => apply(Apply::Down(n)),
            Action::Status => apply(Apply::Status),
        }
    }
}

/// What `up`, `down` and `status` do to the database.
enum Apply {
    Up,
    Down(u32),
    Status,
}

fn apply(what: Apply) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    unlisted()?;
    let config = database()?;
    tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()?.block_on(async {
        // The pool the server opens, and the ORM over it, as the `model`
        // plugin builds it.
        let pool = Db::connect(&config).await?;
        let orm = Orm::from_db(&pool);
        let db = orm.connection();
        let before = Migrator::get_migration_with_status(db).await?;
        let named = |status: MigrationStatus| -> Vec<String> {
            before
                .iter()
                .filter(|m| m.status() == status)
                .map(|m| m.name().to_string())
                .collect()
        };
        match what {
            Apply::Up => {
                let pending = named(MigrationStatus::Pending);
                Migrator::up(db, None).await?;
                if pending.is_empty() {
                    println!("Nothing to apply: each migration is applied.");
                }
                for name in pending {
                    println!("applied      {name}");
                }
            }
            Apply::Down(n) => {
                let applied = named(MigrationStatus::Applied);
                Migrator::down(db, Some(n)).await?;
                if applied.is_empty() {
                    println!("Nothing to roll back: no migration is applied.");
                }
                for name in applied.iter().rev().take(n as usize) {
                    println!("rolled back  {name}");
                }
            }
            Apply::Status => {
                if before.is_empty() {
                    println!("No migration in migrations/.");
                }
                for m in &before {
                    let status = match m.status() {
                        MigrationStatus::Applied => "applied",
                        MigrationStatus::Pending => "pending",
                    };
                    println!("{status:<12} {}", m.name());
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    })
}

/// Runs the `migrate` tool with these arguments, from the project root.
fn tool(args: &[&str]) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let status = std::process::Command::new("cargo")
        .args(["run", "--quiet", "--bin", "migrate", "--"])
        .args(args)
        .status()
        .map_err(|e| {
            anyhow::anyhow!(
                "cannot run cargo: {e}\n\
                 help: run `cargo run --bin migrate -- {}` where cargo is installed",
                args.join(" ")
            )
        })?;
    if !status.success() {
        std::process::exit(status.code().unwrap_or(1));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Refuses when a file in `migrations/` is not in the list this binary was
/// built with: it would be skipped without a word.
fn unlisted() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let built: BTreeSet<String> = Migrator::migrations()
        .iter()
        .map(|m| m.name().to_string())
        .collect();
    let mut missing: Vec<String> = std::fs::read_dir("migrations")
        .map(|dir| {
            dir.flatten()
                .filter_map(|entry| {
                    let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
                    let stem = name.strip_suffix(".rs")?.to_string();
                    (stem.starts_with('m') && stem != "mod" && !built.contains(&stem))
                        .then_some(stem)
                })
                .collect()
        })
        .unwrap_or_default();
    missing.sort();
    if missing.is_empty() {
        return Ok(());
    }
    anyhow::bail!(
        "this binary does not contain {}: migrations/mod.rs does not list it\n\
         help: run `migrate sync` (or `cargo run --bin migrate -- sync`), then run this \
         command again",
        missing.join(", ")
    )
}

/// The pool's configuration: `[db]`, through the loader the server uses, so
/// the files, `$<APP>_ENV` and `$<APP>_DB__URL` agree with what the server
/// sees.
fn database() -> anyhow::Result<DbConfig> {
    let config = brocanth_config::Loader::new(crate::app::APP).load()?;
    Ok(config
        .section::<crate::plugins::db::Settings>("db")?
        .config())
}
===== src/commands/routes.rs =====
//! Every route this application answers.
//!
//! `brocanth routes` builds this project and runs this command, so the
//! listing is the binary's own answer rather than a second reading of the
//! directory. The rows are `crate::pages::handlers()`, read off `src/pages`
//! while the crate compiled: a route is a file, so there is nothing to
//! regenerate and nothing that can fall behind.
//!
//! ```text
//! $ brocanth routes
//! VERB    PATTERN        HANDLER                      TAKES   GIVES
//! GET     /              pages::index::handle         -       -
//! GET     /about         pages::about::handle         -       -
//! POST    /signup        pages::signup::handle_post   Signup  Created
//! ```
//!
//! `TAKES` and `GIVES` are the body a handler reads and the `Json<T>` it
//! returns, from `crate::pages::described()`. A page that writes
//! `-> Result<impl IntoResponse, Error>` says neither, and prints `-`: the
//! wrapper is the opt-in, and these columns report it rather than ask for
//! it.
//!
//! An argument keeps the rows that contain it, in any column, so
//! `routes signup` is the one page and `routes POST` is every route that
//! writes.
//!
//! These are the pages. A plugin that mounts its own routes through a
//! `RouteSource` would not be in the list, and nothing this project has
//! mounts one -- so today the two are the same table. Say so here if that
//! stops being true.

use brocanth_command::{anyhow, clap, cmd, Command, Context};

/// List the routes this application answers.
#[cmd]
#[derive(clap::Args)]
pub struct Routes {
    /// Keep only the rows containing this text
    pub filter: Option<String>,
}

impl Command for Routes {
    fn run(self, _ctx: &mut Context) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let (header, mut rows) = table();
        if let Some(filter) = &self.filter {
            rows.retain(|row| row.iter().any(|cell| cell.contains(filter)));
        }
        if rows.is_empty() {
            // An application with no page and a filter that matched nothing
            // both print nothing, and only one of the two is the reader's
            // own doing.
            match &self.filter {
                Some(filter) => println!("no route matches `{filter}`"),
                None => println!("this application answers no route"),
            }
            return Ok(());
        }

        let mut widths: Vec<usize> = header.iter().map(|title| title.chars().count()).collect();
        for row in &rows {
            for (column, cell) in row.iter().enumerate() {
                widths[column] = widths[column].max(cell.chars().count());
            }
        }

        print_row(&widths, header.iter().copied());
        for row in &rows {
            print_row(&widths, row.iter().map(String::as_str));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// One line, every cell padded to its column but the last.
///
/// The last is left alone, because trailing spaces are invisible until
/// something pipes this into a diff.
fn print_row<'a>(widths: &[usize], cells: impl Iterator<Item = &'a str>) {
    let mut line = String::new();
    for (column, cell) in cells.enumerate() {
        if column > 0 {
            line.push_str("  ");
        }
        if column + 1 == widths.len() {
            line.push_str(cell);
        } else {
            line.push_str(&format!("{cell:<width$}", width = widths[column]));
        }
    }
    println!("{line}");
}

/// The header, and one row per route.
///
/// Five columns, because this project has `input`: `described()` read every
/// handler's signature while the crate compiled, so what a route takes and
/// gives is known here and worth a column.
fn table() -> (Vec<&'static str>, Vec<Vec<String>>) {
    let described = crate::pages::described();
    let rows = crate::pages::handlers()
        .iter()
        .map(|(verb, pattern, handler)| {
            let shape = described
                .iter()
                .find(|row| row.verb == *verb && row.path == *pattern);
            let takes = shape
                .and_then(|row| row.takes.as_ref())
                .and_then(|node| node.name())
                .unwrap_or("-");
            let gives = shape
                .and_then(|row| row.gives.as_ref())
                .and_then(|node| node.name())
                .unwrap_or("-");
            vec![
                verb.as_str().to_string(),
                (*pattern).to_string(),
                format!("pages::{handler}"),
                takes.to_string(),
                gives.to_string(),
            ]
        })
        .collect();
    (vec!["VERB", "PATTERN", "HANDLER", "TAKES", "GIVES"], rows)
}
===== src/pages/about.rsx =====
// The parameters are this page's contract with its handler. Rename one and
// src/pages/about.rs stops compiling, which is the point.

pub fn About(title: &str, verb: &str, path: &str) -> Element {
    <h1>About</h1>
    <p>
        You asked for <code>{verb} {path}</code>. This page answers GET
        and nothing else, so a DELETE to it is a 405 carrying
        an <code>Allow</code> header rather than a 404.
    </p>
    <p>The shell around this is <code>src/pages/layout.rsx</code>, which {title} shares with every page.</p>
}
===== src/pages/index.rsx =====
use crate::pages::views::link::Link;

// The page, and only the page. The document around it is layout.rsx, and
// this file does not know it exists.

pub fn Index(title: &str) -> Element {
    <h1>{title}</h1>
    <p>
        This file is <code>src/pages/index.rsx</code>, beside the handler
        in <code>index.rs</code>, and it is compiled into the binary. Edit it
        and cargo rebuilds; break it and the build stops on the line you broke.
    </p>
    <p>
        An interpolated value is escaped on the way out, always. Writing
        markup verbatim needs a different and greppable hole, so an injection
        is something you can search for rather than something you have to
        remember.
    </p>
    <ul>
        <li><Link to="/about">/about</Link></li>
        <li><Link to={&crate::pages::routes::users::id::path(7)}>User 7</Link></li>
    </ul>
}
===== src/pages/layout.rsx =====
// The document every page in this directory, and every directory below it,
// is rendered inside. A page never names it: which layout wraps a page is a
// property of where the page is, which is the rule the Crystal page_router
// uses for layout.cr.
//
// A layout is an ordinary component with a parameter of type `Element`, and
// `children` is the only parameter `html!` fills -- it cannot know what a
// second one would mean. A value every page shares comes from a const, as
// the title does here; a value belonging to one request belongs on the page
// component, which the handler builds and which already has the context.

use crate::pages::TITLE;

pub fn Layout(layout: &str, children: Element) -> Element {
    <!DOCTYPE html>
    <html lang="en">
        <head>
            <meta charset="utf-8">
            <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
            <title>{TITLE}</title>
            <link rel="stylesheet" href={crate::assets::url("css/site.css")}>
            <script src={crate::assets::url("dpswap.min.js")} defer></script>
        </head>
        <body class="min-h-screen bg-white text-slate-900">
            <header><a href="/">{TITLE}</a></header>
            <main dp-layout={layout} id="outlet">{children}</main>
        </body>
    </html>
}
===== src/pages/link.rsx =====
// An anchor that swaps instead of reloading the document.
//
// Written as a real <a href> and enhanced afterwards. With JavaScript off,
// to a crawler, and on the first load of any page it is a link and the
// browser does what it always did -- which is why `to` is required and why
// there is no version of this that renders a <span> with a click handler.
//
// `to` takes what the route helpers return:
//
//     <Link to={routes::users::id::path(7)}>User 7</Link>
//
// never a string. A route that does not exist is then a compile error
// rather than a 404 somebody finds later.

pub fn Link(to: &str, children: Element) -> Element {
    <a href={to} dp-boost>{children}</a>
}
===== src/pages/openapi.json.rs =====
//! `/openapi.json` -- because the file is called `openapi.json.rs`.
//!
//! The route is the file name, as it is for every page: the last dot is the
//! extension and what is left is the path, so this file answers
//! `/openapi.json` and renaming it moves the document.
//!
//! The body was rendered once, at startup, by `src/plugins/openapi/mod.rs`.
//! This page hands it out and does nothing else.

use crate::pages::{Ctx, Error, IntoResponse};

/// GET `/openapi.json`.
///
/// `no-cache` rather than a long max-age: the document changes when this
/// application is redeployed, and a client holding a stale one is the exact
/// failure a derived document exists to prevent.
pub fn handle(_ctx: &mut Ctx) -> Result<impl IntoResponse, Error> {
    let body = crate::plugins::openapi::json().ok_or_else(|| {
        Error::internal("the openapi plugin is not registered, so there is no document to serve")
    })?;
    Ok((
        body.to_string(),
        200,
        vec![
            ("content-type".to_string(), "application/json".to_string()),
            ("cache-control".to_string(), "no-cache".to_string()),
        ],
    ))
}
===== src/pages/openapi.yaml.rs =====
//! `/openapi.yaml` -- the same document, in the other spelling.
//!
//! Two files and not one handler branching on `Accept`. A route here is a
//! file, so two routes are two files, and a reader who wants only one of
//! them deletes the other.
//!
//! YAML because a person reads this one. The JSON is what a generator
//! consumes; this is what somebody opens to find out whether the endpoint
//! they were promised exists.

use crate::pages::{Ctx, Error, IntoResponse};

/// GET `/openapi.yaml`.
pub fn handle(_ctx: &mut Ctx) -> Result<impl IntoResponse, Error> {
    let body = crate::plugins::openapi::yaml().ok_or_else(|| {
        Error::internal("the openapi plugin is not registered, so there is no document to serve")
    })?;
    Ok((
        body.to_string(),
        200,
        vec![
            ("content-type".to_string(), "application/yaml".to_string()),
            ("cache-control".to_string(), "no-cache".to_string()),
        ],
    ))
}
===== src/pages/realtime/events.rs =====
//! `GET /realtime/events?topics=posts/*,posts/42` -- the broker's frames, as
//! server-sent events.
//!
//! ```js
//! const events = new EventSource("/realtime/events?topics=posts/*");
//! events.addEventListener("posts/*", (e) => console.log(e.data));
//! events.addEventListener("lagged", () => location.reload());
//! ```
//!
//! The topics are in the query because an `EventSource` sends no body and
//! no headers of its own; the cookie goes with it, so a session reads as on
//! any other page. Every topic passes `authorise` before it is filed, and
//! one refusal refuses the request: a stream that quietly follows fewer
//! topics than it asked for is a bug nobody sees.
//!
//! The transport is `crate::plugins::realtime_sse`.

use brocanth_realtime::{Gate, Subscription, Topic};

use crate::pages::{Ctx, Error, IntoResponse, Response};
use crate::plugins::realtime::Broadcast;
use crate::plugins::realtime_sse::Frames;

/// Collections any visitor may follow: every row, every change.
///
/// Empty, so nothing is public until somebody says so here.
const PUBLIC: &[&str] = &[];

/// Whether this request may follow `topic`, and gated by what.
///
/// The one place a topic is authorised, and the place to edit. A public
/// collection takes `Gate::everyone()`. Rows that a policy decides take the
/// policy: `from_policy` gates `posts/*` with the list rule and `posts/42`
/// with the view rule, and the broker inverts the rule into an index key, so
/// a write is a map lookup and not a check per subscriber.
///
/// ```ignore
/// let subject = /* who is asking: the session's user id */;
/// return Ok(Subscription::from_policy(topic, &PostPolicy, &subject));
/// ```
fn authorise(_ctx: &Ctx, topic: Topic) -> Result<Subscription, Error> {
    if PUBLIC.contains(&topic.collection_name()) {
        return Ok(Subscription::new(topic, Gate::everyone()));
    }
    Err(Error::new(
        403,
        format!("no rule lets this request follow {topic}; add one to `authorise` in src/pages/realtime/events.rs"),
    ))
}

pub fn handle(ctx: &mut Ctx) -> Result<impl IntoResponse, Error> {
    let mut subscriptions = Vec::new();
    for topic in topics(&ctx.query)? {
        subscriptions.push(authorise(ctx, topic)?);
    }
    let broker = &ctx
        .provided::<Broadcast, _>()
        .ok_or_else(|| Error::internal("the realtime plugin put no broker on the context"))?
        .broker;

    // A browser that reconnects sends the id of the last frame it read. The
    // broker keeps no history to replay, so the honest answer to "did I miss
    // anything" is yes whenever a frame was published since.
    let missed = ctx
        .header("last-event-id")
        .is_some_and(|seen| seen.trim().parse::<u64>().ok() != Some(broker.last_frame_id()));

    // At the cap the broker refuses rather than evicting somebody. The
    // browser retries on its own; `retry-after` says when.
    let client = broker
        .connect()
        .map_err(|e| Error::new(503, e.to_string()).with_header("retry-after", "5"))?;
    for subscription in subscriptions {
        client
            .subscribe(subscription)
            .map_err(|e| Error::new(400, e.to_string()))?;
    }
    Ok(Response::events(Frames::new(client, missed)))
}

/// Every `topics=` in the query, split at commas and parsed.
fn topics(query: &str) -> Result<Vec<Topic>, Error> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for pair in query.split('&') {
        let Some(("topics", value)) = pair.split_once('=') else {
            continue;
        };
        for text in decoded(value)?.split(',').filter(|t| !t.is_empty()) {
            let topic =
                Topic::parse(text).map_err(|e| Error::new(400, format!("topic {text:?}: {e}")))?;
            out.push(topic);
        }
    }
    if out.is_empty() {
        return Err(Error::new(
            400,
            "name what to follow: ?topics=posts/* for a collection, posts/42 for a row",
        ));
    }
    Ok(out)
}

/// A query value with its `%XX` and `+` undone.
fn decoded(value: &str) -> Result<String, Error> {
    let bad = || {
        Error::new(
            400,
            format!("the query value {value:?} is not percent-encoded UTF-8"),
        )
    };
    let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(value.len());
    let mut rest = value.bytes();
    while let Some(byte) = rest.next() {
        bytes.push(match byte {
            b'+' => b' ',
            b'%' => {
                let hex = [rest.next().ok_or_else(bad)?, rest.next().ok_or_else(bad)?];
                let hex = std::str::from_utf8(&hex).map_err(|_| bad())?;
                u8::from_str_radix(hex, 16).map_err(|_| bad())?
            }
            other => other,
        });
    }
    String::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|_| bad())
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use brocanth::routing::Verb;
    use brocanth_server::Request;

    use super::*;

    async fn status(target: &str) -> u16 {
        let app = crate::app::build().expect("the application builds");
        let (path, query) = target.split_once('?').unwrap_or((target, ""));
        let mut request = Request::new(Verb::Get, path);
        request.query = query.to_string();
        crate::app::handle(&app, request).await.status
    }

    #[test]
    fn topics_are_read_from_the_query_encoded_or_not() {
        let read = topics("topics=posts/*,posts%2F42&x=1&topics=users%2F*").expect("three");
        let names: Vec<String> = read.iter().map(ToString::to_string).collect();
        assert_eq!(names, ["posts/*", "posts/42", "users/*"]);
        assert!(
            topics("").is_err(),
            "no topic is a 400, not a silent stream"
        );
        assert!(topics("topics=posts").is_err(), "a topic has a slash");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_request_without_topics_is_a_bad_request() {
        assert_eq!(status("/realtime/events").await, 400);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_topic_no_rule_allows_is_refused() {
        assert_eq!(status("/realtime/events?topics=posts/*").await, 403);
    }
}
===== src/pages/robots.txt.rs =====
//! `/robots.txt` -- because the file is called `robots.txt.rs`.
//!
//! The text was rendered once, at startup, by `src/plugins/robots/mod.rs`.
//! This page hands it out and does nothing else.

use crate::pages::{Ctx, Error, IntoResponse};

/// GET `/robots.txt`.
///
/// An hour of cache: crawlers keep the file for a day anyway, and an hour
/// is how long a changed rule takes to reach one that asked just before.
pub fn handle(_ctx: &mut Ctx) -> Result<impl IntoResponse, Error> {
    let body = crate::plugins::robots::text().ok_or_else(|| {
        Error::internal("the robots plugin is not registered, so there is no robots.txt to serve")
    })?;
    Ok((
        body.to_string(),
        200,
        vec![
            (
                "content-type".to_string(),
                "text/plain; charset=utf-8".to_string(),
            ),
            ("cache-control".to_string(), "max-age=3600".to_string()),
        ],
    ))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use brocanth::routing::Verb;
    use brocanth_server::Request;

    /// What this project answered the day it was generated. Change the
    /// `[robots]` settings and this line with them.
    const GENERATED: &str = "User-agent: *\nDisallow: /\n";

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn the_application_answers_robots_txt_as_text() {
        let app = crate::app::build().expect("the application builds");
        let response = crate::app::handle(&app, Request::new(Verb::Get, "/robots.txt")).await;
        assert_eq!(response.status, 200);
        assert_eq!(
            response.header("content-type"),
            Some("text/plain; charset=utf-8")
        );
        let body = response.body.bytes().expect("a whole body");
        assert_eq!(std::str::from_utf8(body).expect("utf-8"), GENERATED);
    }
}
===== src/pages/status.jt =====
// The body of `/status`. A template is a function whose body is JSON with
// holes, and the macro compiles it into straight-line writes: every static
// run below is one memcpy, and the commas are resolved while this file is
// compiled rather than counted when a request arrives.
//
// Take parameters by reference. A `&str` is borrowed into the template and
// nothing is copied to render it.

pub fn Status(name: &str, version: &str, parts: &[&str]) -> Json {
    "name": name,
    "version": version,
    "ok": true,
    "parts": [ for p in parts { p } ],
}
===== src/pages/status.rs =====
//! `/status` -- because the file is called `status.rs`.
//!
//! The answer is JSON, and its shape is in `status.jt` beside this file.
//! Nothing here builds a struct for the response: the template is the
//! shape, and it is compiled into the binary rather than parsed per
//! request.

use crate::pages::{payload, render_json, Ctx, Error, IntoResponse};

/// GET. The verb comes off the function name, the same as every other page.
pub fn handle(_ctx: &mut Ctx) -> Result<impl IntoResponse, Error> {
    render_json(payload::status::Status(
        env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME"),
        env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
        &["pages", "router"],
    ))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn the_template_is_the_shape_of_the_answer() {
        // Rendered without a request, because a template takes values and
        // not a context. Edit `status.jt` and this is what changes.
        let body = jt::to_string(&payload::status::Status("api", "0.1.0", &["pages"]));
        assert_eq!(
            body,
            r#"{"name":"api","version":"0.1.0","ok":true,"parts":["pages"]}"#
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_answer_says_it_is_json() {
        let answered = render_json(payload::status::Status("api", "0.1.0", &[])).expect("renders");
        assert!(answered
            .headers
            .iter()
            .any(|(name, value)| name == "content-type" && value == "application/json"));
    }
}
===== src/pages/users/[id].rsx =====
// Two layouts wrap this one: the root, and users/layout.rsx beside it.
// Neither is named here or anywhere else -- `html!` reads the directory
// tree. Delete users/layout.rsx and this page is wrapped in one.

pub fn User(id: u64) -> Element {
    <h1>User {id}</h1>
    <p>
        The <code>id</code> came out of the path. A component takes typed
        parameters, so this one is a <code>u64</code> the whole way
        from <code>src/pages/users/[id].rs</code>, never a string that
        might not be a number.
    </p>
}
===== src/pages/users/layout.rsx =====
// Wraps every page under src/pages/users/, inside the root layout rather
// than instead of it. Nothing declares the stacking: `html!` reads it off
// the directory tree.
//
// `layout` is the URL prefix this layout covers, filled in by `html!`, and
// `dp-layout` is the marker dp-swap walks to find the deepest layer two
// pages share. It goes on the element wrapping exactly the children and
// nothing else: anything inside it is replaced along with them, so a
// sidebar in here would lose its scroll position on every navigation.

pub fn Layout(layout: &str, children: Element) -> Element {
    <section class="users">
        <nav><a href="/">home</a></nav>
        <div dp-layout={layout}>{children}</div>
    </section>
}
===== src/plugins/admin/mod.rs =====
//! The backoffice, at `/admin`.
//!
//! Written once by `brocanth create`. This file is yours.
//!
//! It ships locked, and two answers are yours to give:
//!
//! 1. **Who may open a screen.** The policy is `DenyAll` until
//!    `AdminConfig::with_policy` names another, so every screen answers 403.
//! 2. **Who is asking.** [`principal`] returns an anonymous principal until
//!    it reads your user off the request.
//!
//! It reads rows through the ORM the `model` plugin publishes. A model is in
//! the admin when `models.rs` lists it, and it needs a row policy:
//! `AdminConfig::resource(..)`, one per model. A model with no resource
//! answers 403 on every screen. `brocanth_admin::rows` has the worked
//! example.
//!
//! The routes are in the one table `src/pages/mod.rs` builds:
//! `pages::mounted` calls [`mount`] with the prefix. A page at `/admin` is
//! therefore a build error, not a race.

mod models;

use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, OnceLock, PoisonError};

use brocanth::plugin_api::Plugin;
use brocanth::plugin_context::NoContext;
use brocanth::routing::{BuildError, RouterBuilder, Verb};
use brocanth_admin::policy::Principal;
use brocanth_admin::{Admin, AdminConfig, Fixture, Submission};

use crate::pages::{Ctx, Handler, Response};

/// The admin's titles, its "View site" link and its theme: `[admin]` in
/// the config file, `$<APP>_ADMIN__<KEY>`, or `--admin.<key>`.
///
/// It derives `Deserialize` because this application reads it from
/// `[admin]` in a TOML file. Drop the config plugin and the derive goes
/// with it: `Plugin::Config` carries no bounds the core imposes.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// The end of every `<title>`, and the header and the index heading
    /// when those are not set.
    pub title: String,
    /// What the top of the sidebar says.
    pub header: Option<String>,
    /// The index page's heading.
    pub index_title: Option<String>,
    /// Where the sidebar's "View site" link points. No link when unset.
    pub site_url: Option<String>,
    /// A stylesheet every screen links after the shipped one. More than one
    /// is `AdminConfig::stylesheet` again, in [`mount`].
    pub stylesheet: Option<String>,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            title: "My Blog admin".to_string(),
            header: None,
            index_title: None,
            site_url: None,
            stylesheet: None,
        }
    }
}

/// The settings this run chose, kept for [`mount`].
///
/// `mount` runs when the route table is built, after the plugins are, and
/// takes no argument it could carry them in. A test that builds the table
/// without the application gets the defaults.
static CHOSEN: OnceLock<Settings> = OnceLock::new();

/// Holds the admin's settings. It puts nothing on the context.
pub struct AdminSettings;

impl Plugin for AdminSettings {
    type Config = Settings;
    type Provides = NoContext;
    const NAME: &'static str = "admin";

    fn new(config: Settings) -> Self {
        // The first application built in this process decides.
        let _ = CHOSEN.set(config);
        Self
    }
}

/// Every screen of the admin, under `prefix`.
///
/// Four routes: the index and everything under it, for GET and for POST.
/// The admin parses its own paths, so the table gives it the whole path and
/// does not split it into twelve routes.
pub fn mount(routes: &mut RouterBuilder<Handler>, prefix: &str) -> Result<(), BuildError> {
    let defaults = Settings::default();
    let settings = CHOSEN.get().unwrap_or(&defaults);
    let mut config = AdminConfig::new().titled(&settings.title).at(prefix);
    if let Some(header) = &settings.header {
        config = config.headed(header);
    }
    if let Some(heading) = &settings.index_title {
        config = config.index_titled(heading);
    }
    if let Some(href) = &settings.site_url {
        config = config.site_url(href);
    }
    if let Some(href) = &settings.stylesheet {
        config = config.stylesheet(href);
    }
    // The page views the analytics plugin counts, as a tab.
    config = config.panel(brocanth_analytics::admin::AnalyticsPanel::installed());
    // Built by the first request, over the ORM: see `OverOrm`.
    let admin = Arc::new(OverOrm::new(config));
    let rest = format!("{}/{{*rest}}", prefix.trim_end_matches('/'));
    for pattern in [prefix, rest.as_str()] {
        routes.route(pattern, Verb::Get, screen(Arc::clone(&admin)))?;
        routes.route(pattern, Verb::Post, screen(Arc::clone(&admin)))?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The admin over the ORM, built once, by the first request.
///
/// `mount` runs when the route table is built, and the plugins start after
/// that: the `db` plugin opens the pool in `before_start`, and the `model`
/// plugin wraps it. So the admin cannot be built in `mount`. The first
/// request after the start carries the ORM on its context, and the admin is
/// built from it then. A row policy for a model that is not listed therefore
/// panics on that first request, not at startup.
///
/// One per route table. The table `src/app.rs` builds only ever sees a
/// request the application dispatched. A table a test builds sees a `Ctx`
/// built by hand, which has no ORM: that admin is built over an empty
/// source, with the same configuration, and shows no rows.
struct OverOrm {
    config: Mutex<Option<AdminConfig>>,
    built: OnceLock<Arc<Admin>>,
}

impl OverOrm {
    fn new(config: AdminConfig) -> Self {
        Self {
            config: Mutex::new(Some(config)),
            built: OnceLock::new(),
        }
    }

    /// The admin, built by the first request that asks.
    fn for_request(&self, ctx: &Ctx) -> Arc<Admin> {
        Arc::clone(self.built.get_or_init(|| {
            let config = self
                .config
                .lock()
                .unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
                .take()
                .expect("the admin is built once");
            match ctx.provided::<brocanth_model::Orm, _>() {
                Some(orm) => Arc::new(Admin::new(
                    Arc::new(models::Models::new(orm.connection().clone())),
                    config,
                )),
                None => Arc::new(Admin::new(Arc::new(Fixture::new()), config)),
            }
        }))
    }
}

/// One handler for every screen. The admin reads the path and decides.
///
/// The admin is async because a database is, and so is a handler in this
/// table: the answer is awaited and holds no thread while it waits.
fn screen(admin: Arc<OverOrm>) -> Handler {
    Box::new(move |ctx: &mut Ctx| {
        let admin = Arc::clone(&admin);
        Box::pin(async move {
            let ctx = &*ctx;
            let admin = admin.for_request(ctx);
            // HEAD reaches the GET handler, and the admin knows two verbs.
            let method = match ctx.verb {
                Verb::Post => "POST",
                _ => "GET",
            };
            let form = submission(ctx);
            let who = principal(ctx);
