            });
        }
    }
}
===== src/plugins/realtime_sse/mod.rs =====
//! `realtime-sse`: the broker's frames, written to a browser as server-sent
//! events.
//!
//! The transport is here, in the application, and not in
//! `brocanth-realtime`, because that crate does not depend on `brocanth`:
//! nothing in it touches a request, a response or a route. A transport is a
//! response body, and a body belongs to the crate that owns the routes, which
//! is this one. `src/pages/realtime/events.rs` is the route.
//!
//! # What the stream writes
//!
//! ```text
//! : connected 7              first, so the headers leave at once
//! event:lagged               first, when a reconnect may have missed frames
//! id:12 event:posts/* data:  each frame the broker addressed to this client
//! event:lagged data:3        the mailbox was full and 3 frames were dropped
//! :                          a heartbeat, after HEARTBEAT with nothing to say
//! event:close                the server is stopping; the browser reconnects
//! ```
//!
//! `lagged` means "what you show may be stale: fetch it again". It is the
//! mailbox's `Event::Lagged`, written for the browser.
//!
//! # Back-pressure
//!
//! The broker never waits for this stream. The mailbox is bounded, and
//! `[realtime] overflow` says what a full one does. `drop-oldest` and
//! `drop-newest` drop frames, and the stream writes `lagged`. `disconnect`
//! closes the mailbox, the stream ends, and the browser reconnects with
//! `Last-Event-ID` and is told `lagged`.
//!
//! # Ending
//!
//! * The browser leaves. The server drops this stream, which drops the
//!   `Client`, which unsubscribes it and closes its mailbox. The server
//!   learns that a socket is gone only when a write fails, so the heartbeat
//!   is also what frees a dead subscriber, within one period.
//! * The server stops. The stream gate calls `finish`. The stream writes the
//!   frames already queued, then `event:close`, and ends, so a deploy does
//!   not wait for a subscriber.

use std::task::{Context, Poll};
use std::time::Duration;

use brocanth::plugin_body::{BodyStream, Chunk};
use brocanth_realtime::{Client, Event};
use tokio::time::{Instant, Interval, MissedTickBehavior};

/// How long a stream stays silent before it writes a heartbeat.
///
/// Shorter than the idle timeout of any proxy in front of this server, and
/// the longest a dead subscriber holds its mailbox.
pub const HEARTBEAT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(15);

/// One subscriber's frames, as a response body.
pub struct Frames {
    /// The broker's handle for this connection. Dropped with the stream, and
    /// that drop is the disconnect.
    client: Client,
    /// Written before the first frame.
    preamble: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    /// What `finish` left to write: the queued frames and `event:close`.
    tail: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    ended: bool,
    /// Built on the first idle poll: a timer needs the runtime, and the
    /// server's poll is certain to have one.
    ticker: Option<Interval>,
}

impl Frames {
    /// A stream over `client`'s mailbox.
    ///
    /// `missed` is true when the browser reconnected and frames were
    /// published since the last one it read. The broker keeps no history, so
    /// the stream cannot replay them; it says `lagged` instead.
    pub fn new(client: Client, missed: bool) -> Self {
        let mut preamble = format!(": connected {}\n\n", client.id()).into_bytes();
        if missed {
            preamble.extend_from_slice(&lagged(None));
        }
        Self {
            client,
            preamble: Some(preamble),
            tail: None,
            ended: false,
            ticker: None,
        }
    }
}

/// `event:lagged`, with how many frames were dropped when that is known.
fn lagged(skipped: Option<u64>) -> Vec<u8> {
    match skipped {
        Some(n) => format!("event:lagged\ndata:{n}\n\n").into_bytes(),
        None => b"event:lagged\ndata:\n\n".to_vec(),
    }
}

/// What a mailbox event looks like on the wire.
fn encoded(event: Event) -> Vec<u8> {
    match event {
        // Encoded once by the broker and shared by every subscriber.
        Event::Frame(frame) => frame.bytes().to_vec(),
        Event::Lagged { skipped } => lagged(Some(skipped)),
    }
}

impl BodyStream for Frames {
    fn poll_chunk(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Chunk {
        if let Some(preamble) = self.preamble.take() {
            return Poll::Ready(Some(Ok(preamble)));
        }
        if let Some(tail) = self.tail.take() {
            self.ended = true;
            return Poll::Ready(Some(Ok(tail)));
        }
        if self.ended {
            return Poll::Ready(None);
        }
        match self.client.mailbox().poll_recv(cx) {
            Poll::Ready(Some(event)) => {
                // A frame is traffic, so the next heartbeat is a full
                // period away.
                if let Some(ticker) = &mut self.ticker {
                    ticker.reset();
                }
                return Poll::Ready(Some(Ok(encoded(event))));
            }
            // This stream holds the client, so only the overflow policy
            // closes its mailbox: `disconnect` fired. End; the browser comes
            // back with `Last-Event-ID` and is told `lagged`.
            Poll::Ready(None) => return Poll::Ready(None),
            Poll::Pending => {}
        }
        let ticker = self.ticker.get_or_insert_with(|| {
            let mut ticker = tokio::time::interval_at(Instant::now() + HEARTBEAT, HEARTBEAT);
            ticker.set_missed_tick_behavior(MissedTickBehavior::Delay);
            ticker
        });
        match ticker.poll_tick(cx) {
            Poll::Ready(_) => Poll::Ready(Some(Ok(b":\n\n".to_vec()))),
            Poll::Pending => Poll::Pending,
        }
    }

    /// The server is stopping: write what is queued, then `event:close`.
    fn finish(&mut self) {
        let mut tail = Vec::new();
        for event in self.client.mailbox().drain() {
            tail.extend(encoded(event));
        }
        tail.extend_from_slice(b"event:close\ndata:\n\n");
        self.tail = Some(tail);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use brocanth_events::RowChange;
    use brocanth_realtime::{Broker, Gate, Subscription, Topic};

    use super::*;

    async fn next(frames: &mut Frames) -> Option<String> {
        let chunk = std::future::poll_fn(|cx| frames.poll_chunk(cx)).await?;
        Some(String::from_utf8(chunk.expect("no error")).expect("utf-8"))
    }

    fn subscribed(broker: &std::sync::Arc<Broker>) -> Client {
        let client = broker.connect().expect("room");
        client
            .subscribe(Subscription::new(
                Topic::collection("posts").expect("a topic"),
                Gate::everyone(),
            ))
            .expect("subscribed");
        client
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_published_change_is_written_as_an_event() {
        let broker = Broker::new();
        let mut frames = Frames::new(subscribed(&broker), false);
        assert_eq!(
            next(&mut frames).await.as_deref(),
            Some(": connected 1\n\n")
        );

        broker.publish_change(&RowChange::created("posts", 42i64));
        let frame = next(&mut frames).await.expect("a frame");
        assert!(frame.starts_with("id:1\nevent:posts/*\n"), "{frame}");
        assert!(frame.contains("data:id=42\n"), "{frame}");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_reconnect_that_missed_frames_is_told_so() {
        let broker = Broker::new();
        let mut frames = Frames::new(subscribed(&broker), true);
        let preamble = next(&mut frames).await.expect("the preamble");
        assert!(preamble.ends_with("event:lagged\ndata:\n\n"), "{preamble}");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn finish_writes_the_queue_then_close_then_ends() {
        let broker = Broker::new();
        let mut frames = Frames::new(subscribed(&broker), false);
        let _ = next(&mut frames).await;
        broker.publish_change(&RowChange::deleted("posts", 7i64));

        frames.finish();
        let tail = next(&mut frames).await.expect("the tail");
        assert!(tail.contains("data:id=7\n"), "{tail}");
        assert!(tail.ends_with("event:close\ndata:\n\n"), "{tail}");
        assert_eq!(next(&mut frames).await, None);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn dropping_the_stream_frees_the_subscriber() {
        let broker = Broker::new();
        let frames = Frames::new(subscribed(&broker), false);
        assert_eq!(broker.clients(), 1);
        drop(frames);
        assert_eq!(broker.clients(), 0);
    }
}
===== src/plugins/resource/mod.rs =====
//! Typed CRUD routes over your tables, with the policy in the `WHERE` clause.
//!
//! Written once by `brocanth create`. This file is yours.
//!
//! [`mount`] is the list of resources this application serves, and it starts
//! empty: a resource is one table, and a new project has none. Add one line
//! per resource. A resource is a `brocanth_resource::Resource`: an entity, a
//! policy over its rows (there is no default, so a resource without one does
//! not compile), a data source and three conversions. That crate's own
//! documentation has the worked example.
//!
//! `src/pages/mod.rs` calls [`mount`] at `/api`, so every route lands in the
//! one table. A page and a resource that claim one path are a build error.
//!
//! The three impls below make this project's `Ctx`, `Response` and `Error`
//! the page triple `brocanth_resource::pages` is written against. A resource
//! also implements `PageSubject<Ctx>`, which reads who is asking off a
//! request.

use brocanth::routing::{BuildError, RouterBuilder};
use brocanth_resource::pages::{PageCtx, PageError, PageResponse};

use crate::pages::{Ctx, Error, Handler, Response};

/// Every resource, under `prefix`.
///
/// Seven routes each: the five REST routes, and `POST /{id}` and
/// `POST /{id}/delete` for an HTML form, which can send nothing but GET and
/// POST. `brocanth_resource::pages::mount_api` mounts the five alone.
///
/// ```ignore
/// brocanth_resource::pages::mount(routes, &format!("{prefix}/posts"), Arc::new(Posts::new()))?;
/// ```
pub fn mount(routes: &mut RouterBuilder<Handler>, prefix: &str) -> Result<(), BuildError> {
    let _ = (routes, prefix);
    Ok(())
}

impl PageCtx for Ctx {
    fn query(&self) -> &str {
        &self.query
    }

    fn body(&self) -> &[u8] {
        &self.body
    }

    fn param(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        Ctx::param(self, name)
    }

    fn header(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        Ctx::header(self, name)
    }
}

impl PageResponse for Response {
    fn page_response(status: u16, body: String, headers: Vec<(String, String)>) -> Self {
        Response {
            status,
            body,
            headers,
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }
}

impl PageError for Error {
    fn page_error(status: u16, message: String) -> Self {
        Error::new(status, message)
    }
}
===== src/plugins/robots/mod.rs =====
//! The robots.txt, as this application answers it.
//!
//! Rendered once at startup from `Settings`, then served by
//! `src/pages/robots.txt.rs`. A rule path that does not start with `/`, or
//! a sitemap that is not a full URL, stops the build here: a crawler would
//! ignore that line, and the page it was meant to hide would be indexed.
//!
//! `index = false` answers `User-agent: *` / `Disallow: /` and nothing
//! else. That is the answer for development and staging.
//!
//! Only the root `/robots.txt` of a host is read. Under a base path, as on
//! a GitHub Pages project site, crawlers never ask for this file.

use std::sync::OnceLock;

use brocanth::plugin_api::{Lifecycle, Plugin, PluginError};
use brocanth::plugin_context::NoContext;
use brocanth_robots::{Group, Robots as Text};

/// The rendered text, set once at `configure`.
static RENDERED: OnceLock<String> = OnceLock::new();

/// The text, or `None` when this plugin was never registered.
pub fn text() -> Option<&'static str> {
    RENDERED.get().map(String::as_str)
}

/// What this plugin is built from.
///
/// It derives `Deserialize` because this application reads it from
/// `[robots]` in a TOML file. Drop the config plugin and the derive goes
/// with it: `Plugin::Config` carries no bounds the core imposes.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// Let crawlers read this site.
    pub index: bool,
    /// Paths no crawler may read.
    pub disallow: Vec<String>,
    /// Paths a crawler may read under a disallowed one.
    pub allow: Vec<String>,
    /// Where the sitemap is, as a full URL.
    pub sitemap: Option<String>,
    /// Groups for named crawlers, written after the `*` group. File-only:
    /// `[[robots.groups]]`.
    pub groups: Vec<CrawlerGroup>,
}

/// One `[[robots.groups]]` table.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct CrawlerGroup {
    /// The crawlers this group names, by product token: "GPTBot".
    pub agents: Vec<String>,
    /// Paths these crawlers may read under a disallowed one.
    pub allow: Vec<String>,
    /// Paths these crawlers may not read.
    pub disallow: Vec<String>,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    /// Open: a production server with no `[robots]` section is indexed.
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            index: true,
            disallow: vec!["/admin".to_string()],
            allow: Vec::new(),
            sitemap: None,
            groups: Vec::new(),
        }
    }
}

pub struct Robots {
    settings: Settings,
}

impl Robots {
    /// The builder these settings describe.
    fn text(&self) -> Result<Text, PluginError> {
        if !self.settings.index {
            return Ok(Text::closed());
        }
        let mut text = Text::new();
        for path in &self.settings.disallow {
            text = text.disallow(path.as_str());
        }
        for path in &self.settings.allow {
            text = text.allow(path.as_str());
        }
        for named in &self.settings.groups {
            let Some((first, rest)) = named.agents.split_first() else {
                return Err(PluginError::new(
                    "[robots] a [[robots.groups]] table names no crawler\n\
                     help: give it agents = [\"GPTBot\"], or delete the table",
                ));
            };
            let mut group = Group::new(first.as_str());
            for agent in rest {
                group = group.agent(agent.as_str());
            }
            for path in &named.disallow {
                group = group.disallow(path.as_str());
            }
            for path in &named.allow {
                group = group.allow(path.as_str());
            }
            text = text.group(group);
        }
        if let Some(url) = &self.settings.sitemap {
            text = text.sitemap(url.as_str());
        }
        Ok(text)
    }

    /// The text these settings describe, or why it cannot be served.
    fn rendered(&self) -> Result<String, PluginError> {
        self.text()?
            .render()
            .map_err(|e| PluginError::new(format!("[robots] {e}")))
    }
}

impl Plugin for Robots {
    type Config = Settings;
    type Provides = NoContext;
    const NAME: &'static str = "robots";

    fn new(config: Settings) -> Self {
        Self { settings: config }
    }

    fn configure(&mut self, _lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let _ = RENDERED.set(self.rendered()?);
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn ai_crawlers() -> CrawlerGroup {
        CrawlerGroup {
            agents: vec!["GPTBot".to_string(), "CCBot".to_string()],
            disallow: vec!["/".to_string()],
            ..CrawlerGroup::default()
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn closed_settings_answer_disallow_everything_and_nothing_else() {
        let robots = Robots::new(Settings {
            index: false,
            groups: vec![ai_crawlers()],
            ..Settings::default()
        });
        assert_eq!(robots.rendered().unwrap(), "User-agent: *\nDisallow: /\n");
    }

    #[test]
    fn open_settings_write_each_rule_then_each_group() {
        let robots = Robots::new(Settings {
            disallow: vec!["/private".to_string()],
            allow: vec!["/private/help".to_string()],
            sitemap: Some("https://example.com/sitemap.xml".to_string()),
            groups: vec![ai_crawlers()],
            ..Settings::default()
        });
        let text = robots.rendered().unwrap();
        assert!(text.contains("Disallow: /private\n"), "{text}");
        assert!(text.contains("Allow: /private/help\n"), "{text}");
        assert!(
            text.contains("\nUser-agent: GPTBot\nUser-agent: CCBot\nDisallow: /\n"),
            "{text}"
        );
        assert!(
            text.ends_with("Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml\n"),
            "{text}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_group_with_no_crawler_stops_the_build() {
        let robots = Robots::new(Settings {
            groups: vec![CrawlerGroup::default()],
            ..Settings::default()
        });
        let error = robots.rendered().unwrap_err().to_string();
        assert!(error.contains("help:"), "{error}");
    }
}
===== src/plugins/sessions/mod.rs =====
//! Cookie sessions, and the one value they put on the context.

use brocanth::plugin_api::{Lifecycle, MiddlewareCatalog, Plugin, PluginError};
use brocanth::plugin_context::{ContextBuilder, ContextItem, ProvidesContext};
use brocanth::plugin_routes::BoxFuture;
use brocanth::routing::AsyncNext;

use crate::pages::{Ctx, Response};

/// What this plugin is built from.
///
/// It derives `Deserialize` because this application reads it from
/// `[sessions]` in a TOML file. Drop the config plugin and the derive goes
/// with it: `Plugin::Config` carries no bounds the core imposes.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    pub cookie: String,
    /// `Secure`, so the cookie never leaves over plain HTTP. False in
    /// development and nowhere else.
    pub secure: bool,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            cookie: "_my_blog_session".to_string(),
            secure: true,
        }
    }
}

/// What this plugin puts on the context.
///
/// One provider owns one type, so there is no string name to misspell and no
/// `responds_to?` guard to forget. A handler that asks for a `Session` in an
/// application that never registered this plugin does not compile.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct Session {
    pub cookie: String,
}

impl ContextItem for Session {}

pub struct Sessions {
    cookie: String,
    secure: bool,
}

impl Plugin for Sessions {
    type Config = Settings;
    type Provides = ProvidesContext<Session>;
    const NAME: &'static str = "sessions";

    fn new(config: Settings) -> Self {
        Self {
            cookie: config.cookie,
            secure: config.secure,
        }
    }

    fn configure(&mut self, _lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        if self.cookie.is_empty() {
            // A missing or ill-typed key fails at startup, not at first use,
            // and the plugin never quietly chooses a name the operator did not.
            return Err(PluginError::new("[sessions] cookie must not be empty"));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn configure_router(&mut self, catalog: &mut MiddlewareCatalog<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        catalog.offer(
            "session",
            "reads the cookie and puts a Session on the context",
        );
        Ok(())
    }

    fn before_start(&mut self, _lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        if !self.secure {
            crate::plugins::say!(warn, "[sessions] Secure is off: development only");
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn provide(&self, cx: &mut ContextBuilder) {
        cx.insert(Session {
            cookie: self.cookie.clone(),
        });
    }
}

/// The layer `session` mounts. Reading the cookie off the request and writing
/// `Set-Cookie` on the way out both need the request type that arrives with the
/// HTTP server; the seam is here and it is already the right shape.
///
/// A layer may wait, which is what a session store wants: the lookup is
/// awaited here and holds no thread.
pub fn layer<'a>(ctx: &'a mut Ctx, next: AsyncNext<'a, Ctx, Response>) -> BoxFuture<'a, Response> {
    next.run(ctx)
}
===== src/plugins/storage/mod.rs =====
//! File storage, as this application registers it.
//!
//! An object is named by what is in it. Thirty-two bytes rendered as
//! sixty-four hex characters is the whole address, so `..`, a slash and a
//! drive letter are not values the type can hold and no filename a client
//! sent ever becomes a path component. The original name is kept as metadata,
//! defanged for the `Content-Disposition` header it ends up in, and never
//! touches the filesystem.
//!
//! `brocanth-storage` is in `Cargo.toml` because this file is here, and
//! through no other route. Delete the registration in `src/app.rs` and delete
//! this file, and the application stores no files and links nothing to store
//! them with.
//!
//! # Uploading
//!
//! There is no upload route here, on purpose: `brocanth-storage` parses no
//! multipart body and knows nothing about HTTP, and whether *this*
//! application lets *this* request store a file is a policy question a
//! generator cannot answer. A handler that has already asked it writes:
//!
//! ```ignore
//! let files = ctx.provided::<FileStore, _>().expect("a dispatched request");
//! let about = ObjectInfo::new()
//!     .with_filename(sent_name)
//!     .with_declared_type(sent_type);
//! let key = files.store.put(&bytes, &about).await?;
//! ```
//!
//! and keeps `key.to_hex()` on the record. The media type is taken from the
//! bytes rather than from `sent_type`, because a client that labels a file
//! `text/html` is choosing what this origin serves back to the next visitor.
//!
//! # Serving
//!
//! Also the application's, and for a sharper reason: a file token says "the
//! bearer may read this object" and carries no identity at all. Mint one only
//! for a request that has already passed the policy, because after that the
//! token is the only thing between the object and whoever the URL reaches.
//!
//! ```ignore
//! let token = files.tokens.issue(&key);           // after the policy said yes
//! let key = files.tokens.verify(presented)?;      // on the download route
//! let meta = files.store.meta(&key).await?;
//! ```
//!
//! `ObjectMeta::content_type` answers `is_safe_to_inline`, which is the bit
//! the download route needs to force an attachment for everything that is not
//! a recognised image.
//!
//! # Thumbnails
//!
//! `get_variant` and `put_variant` are here already, with the `variants`
//! feature off: moving derived bytes needs no codec, so this build can serve
//! a variant another process computed and cannot compute one itself. Turning
//! the feature on in `Cargo.toml` adds `derive_variant`, and adds png, jpeg,
//! gif and webp decoders pointed at stranger-supplied bytes. An application
//! that stores documents should leave it off.
//!
//! # One secret, two keys
//!
//! `secret` below is used twice and the two uses cannot be confused for each
//! other: `HashKey` and `FileTokenKey` derive from it under different domain
//! separators, so an address key cannot sign a token and a token key cannot
//! address an object. Rotating the secret invalidates every outstanding token
//! at once, which is the break-glass, and it also changes the address new
//! uploads are stored at -- objects already on disk keep the address they
//! were written under, so rotate it with a plan rather than on a Friday.

use std::sync::Arc;

use brocanth::plugin_api::{Lifecycle, Plugin, PluginError};
use brocanth::plugin_context::{ContextBuilder, ContextItem, ProvidesContext};
use brocanth_storage::{FileTokenKey, FileTokens, HashKey, LocalDisk, Storage};

/// What this plugin is built from.
///
/// It derives `Deserialize` because this application reads it from
/// `[storage]` in a TOML file. Drop the config plugin and the derive goes
/// with it: `Plugin::Config` carries no bounds the core imposes.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// Where the objects live, relative to the working directory or absolute.
    /// Created if it is not there.
    pub root: String,
    /// The deployment secret. It signs file tokens and keys object addresses;
    /// see the module header for what each of those means.
    pub secret: String,
    /// How many seconds a file token lives. A token cannot be revoked, so
    /// this is the leak window.
    pub token_ttl: i64,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            root: "var/uploads".to_string(),
            secret: "development only: replace before anything is uploaded in anger".to_string(),
            token_ttl: 120,
        }
    }
}

/// What this plugin puts on the context.
///
/// A wrapper and not the two values loose, because `ContextItem` is
/// brocanth's trait and both of these are `brocanth-storage`'s types. That
/// crate deliberately does not depend on the core -- it has no routes, parses
/// no multipart body and knows nothing about HTTP -- so the impl that joins
/// the two belongs in the one crate that can see both, which is this one.
pub struct FileStore {
    /// The store, behind the trait rather than as a `LocalDisk`, so swapping
    /// the backend is a change in this file and nowhere else.
    ///
    /// Allowed to be unread, and only until one thing changes. Every
    /// `Storage` method is `async` and the startup line below is not, so
    /// nothing the generator writes can touch this field — a handler is
    /// what uses it, and a handler cannot reach the per-request context
    /// yet, because `Ctx` in `src/pages/mod.rs` has no extractor. Delete
    /// this attribute the moment you write the first upload route; it is
    /// a note about today, not about the field.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub store: Arc<dyn Storage>,
    /// Mints and verifies the short-lived tokens a download route checks.
    pub tokens: FileTokens,
}

impl ContextItem for FileStore {}

pub struct Files {
    settings: Settings,
    /// Built at `configure`, because opening a store can fail and
    /// `Plugin::new` cannot.
    store: Option<Arc<dyn Storage>>,
    tokens: Option<FileTokens>,
}

impl Plugin for Files {
    type Config = Settings;
    type Provides = ProvidesContext<FileStore>;
    const NAME: &'static str = "storage";

    fn new(config: Settings) -> Self {
        Self {
            settings: config,
            store: None,
            tokens: None,
        }
    }

    fn configure(&mut self, _lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        if self.settings.root.is_empty() {
            return Err(PluginError::new(
                "[storage] root is required; there is no default directory",
            ));
        }
        if self.settings.secret.is_empty() {
            // An empty secret is not a weaker store, it is two different
            // stores: addresses stop being keyed, and a token key of no bytes
            // signs tokens anybody can forge.
            return Err(PluginError::new(
                "[storage] secret is required; it signs file tokens and keys object addresses",
            ));
        }
        if self.settings.token_ttl <= 0 {
            return Err(PluginError::new(
                "[storage] token_ttl must be at least one second, or no token is ever valid",
            ));
        }
        // Synchronous: `std::fs`, a `create_dir_all` and a `canonicalize`.
        // Unlike a pool there is nothing to open, so there is no
        // `before_start`.
        let disk = LocalDisk::open(&self.settings.root)
            .map_err(|e| {
                PluginError::new(format!("[storage] opening {:?}: {e}", self.settings.root))
            })?
            .with_hash_key(HashKey::from_secret(self.settings.secret.as_bytes()));
        self.store = Some(Arc::new(disk));
        self.tokens = Some(
            FileTokens::new(FileTokenKey::from_secret(self.settings.secret.as_bytes()))
                .with_ttl(self.settings.token_ttl),
        );
        Ok(())
    }

    fn provide(&self, cx: &mut ContextBuilder) {
        // `configure` runs before the server is handed the application, so
        // both are here by the time any request builds a context.
        if let (Some(store), Some(tokens)) = (&self.store, &self.tokens) {
            cx.insert(FileStore {
                store: store.clone(),
                tokens: tokens.clone(),
            });
        }
    }
}
===== src/plugins/validation/mod.rs =====
//! Request validation, as this application registers it.
//!
//! The shape of a schema is checked when this crate compiles; the data is
//! checked when a request arrives, because a request body is bytes that did
//! not exist at compile time. What the derive buys is that the check and the
//! description come from one declaration, so a form, an OpenAPI document and
//! the check on the way in cannot drift apart.
//!
//! `brocanth-schema` is in `Cargo.toml` because this file is here, and
//! through no other route. Delete the registration in `src/app.rs` and delete
//! this file, and the application validates nothing and links nothing to
//! validate with.
//!
//! # The proof, and why a handler asks for it
//!
//! `Valid<T>` has a private field and exactly one constructor:
//! `Validation::check`, a method on the context item this plugin provides.
//! A handler that takes a `Valid<SignUp>` therefore has proof the body was
//! checked, and a handler in an application that never registered this plugin
//! does not compile. Forgetting to wire validation is a build that does not
//! finish rather than a bug that reaches production.
//!
//! ```ignore
//! let checks = ctx
//!     .provided::<brocanth_schema::Validation, _>()
//!     .expect("a dispatched request");
//! match checks.check(SignUp { username, email }) {
//!     Ok(body) => create(body),
//!     Err(issues) => Response {
//!         status: 422,
//!         body: checks.render(&issues),
//!         ..Default::default()
//!     },
//! }
//! ```
//!
//! # Where schemas go
//!
//! `SignUp` is here so that this file compiles into something that runs. Move
//! it, and whatever follows it, into `src/schemas/` once there is more than
//! one. Nothing registers a schema: a type with `#[derive(Validate)]` is
//! reachable from wherever it is written.
//!
//! # The middleware this does not mount
//!
//! `ValidationPlugin` offers a middleware called `validation.report`, and
//! this plugin does not pass the offer on. The offer is a name; the crate
//! ships no function behind it, because turning an unhandled report into a
//! 422 means knowing what this application's `Response` is. Mounting a name
//! with no layer behind it stops the application at startup, so the offer is
//! withheld until there is something to mount. Write the layer in this file,
//! add `"validation.report" => Some(validation::layer),` to
//! `src/plugins/mod.rs`, and forward `configure_router` to `self.inner`.

use brocanth::plugin_api::{Lifecycle, Plugin, PluginError};
use brocanth::plugin_context::{ContextBuilder, ProvidesContext};
use brocanth_schema::{ReportStyle, Validate, ValidationConfig, ValidationPlugin};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A schema
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// What somebody may send to sign up.
///
/// A constraint that cannot mean anything for a field's type does not
/// compile, and neither does a rule naming a field this struct does not have:
/// the derive reads the field list from the struct, so there is no string to
/// misspell.
#[derive(Debug, Validate)]
/// The shape a sign-up body has to have.
///
/// Allowed to be unconstructed: a handler is what builds one, and a
/// handler cannot reach the per-request context yet — `Ctx` in
/// `src/pages/mod.rs` has no extractor, so `Valid<SignUp>` has nowhere to
/// be asked for. Delete this attribute with the first route that takes a
/// body.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub struct SignUp {
    /// Three to thirty-two characters.
    #[validate(string(min_length = 3, max_length = 32))]
    pub username: String,
    /// Checked against the shape of an address, not against a mail server.
    #[validate(string(email))]
    pub email: String,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The plugin
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// What this plugin is built from.
///
/// It derives `Deserialize` because this application reads it from
/// `[validation]` in a TOML file. Drop the config plugin and the derive goes
/// with it: `Plugin::Config` carries no bounds the core imposes.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// `json` or `form`. A string here and an enum below: the config file is
    /// text, and the translation is checked at startup where a typo can still
    /// be answered.
    pub report: String,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            report: "json".to_string(),
        }
    }
}

pub struct Validation {
    report: String,
    /// Built at `configure` and not in `new`, because reading the report
    /// style out of a string can fail and `Plugin::new` cannot.
    inner: Option<ValidationPlugin>,
}

impl Plugin for Validation {
    type Config = Settings;
    type Provides = ProvidesContext<brocanth_schema::Validation>;
    const NAME: &'static str = "validation";

    fn new(config: Settings) -> Self {
        Self {
            report: config.report,
            inner: None,
        }
    }

    fn configure(&mut self, _lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let report = match self.report.as_str() {
            "json" => ReportStyle::Json,
            "form" => ReportStyle::Form,
            other => {
                return Err(PluginError::new(format!(
                    "[validation] report is {other:?}; write json or form"
                )))
            }
        };
        // The crate's own plugin, held rather than registered: it is the only
        // thing that can build the context item, because `Validation`'s field
        // is private and this file is not that crate.
        self.inner = Some(ValidationPlugin::new(ValidationConfig { report }));
        Ok(())
    }

    fn provide(&self, cx: &mut ContextBuilder) {
        // `configure` runs before the server is handed the application, so
        // the inner plugin is here by the time any request builds a context.
        if let Some(inner) = &self.inner {
            inner.provide(cx);
        }
    }
}
===== AGENTS.md =====
<!-- Written by `brocanth`. Do not edit -- `brocanth add` rewrites this file. -->
<!-- Notes of your own go in a file of your own, beside this one. -->
# Working in My Blog

A brief for a coding agent. Written by `brocanth`, so the lists
below are this project's and not the framework's in general.

## Check your work

Run these after every change, in this order. They are ordered by how
fast they fail.

```
cargo test
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check
```

The route table is `pages::router()` and the test beside it asserts the
shape of the directory. Read it rather than guessing what covers a
request.

## What this binary contains

- `core`  the router, the context, the plugin seams
- `observability`  a request id on every request and a SIGTERM that fails /readyz first; logs, probes, metrics and traces below
- `observability-logs`  the production log: JSON on stdout in production, text elsewhere, with request id, duration and spans
- `observability-health`  /up for liveness, /readyz runs every plugin's check and fails first on SIGTERM
- `observability-metrics`  Prometheus text on /metrics: requests by route and status, in-flight, job queues
- `observability-tracing`  an OTLP span per request and per job, W3C traceparent in and out; needs a collector
- `analytics`  page views counted on the server: no cookie, no script, no third party; rows in your Postgres
- `config`  config/<env>.toml, merged; without it nothing links a TOML parser
- `sessions`  a cookie, and a `Session` the context hands a handler
- `db`  one Postgres pool and sea-query statements, read as ctx.db(); without it no SQL driver
- `model`  SeaORM, validations, migrations, over the `db` pool
- `cache`  a cache on an unlogged Postgres table, not Redis; without it no cache at all
- `jobs`  a queue in Postgres with retries and a dead letter; a worker in this process
- `auth`  argon2id accounts and signed sessions; no provider, so no HTTP client
- `policy`  typed predicates over an entity's columns; no ORM, no driver, no core
- `storage`  uploads on a local disk, addressed by content hash; no object store and no S3
- `input`  a form or a JSON body, read into a struct, with every fault at once
- `client`  a subcommand that calls this application's own API, built from its routes
- `middleware`  proxy headers, method override, canonical host, content types, CORS
- `middleware-csrf`  a double-submit cookie, checked on every verb that is not a read
- `middleware-security-headers`  HSTS, nosniff, a referrer policy, no framing, a CSP that runs dp-swap by hash
- `middleware-rate-limit`  a fixed window per address, session or user, per group of routes; 429 with Retry-After
- `gtag`  Google Analytics 4 behind a consent banner; nothing leaves before the visitor accepts
- `openapi`  an OpenAPI 3.1 document derived from src/pages, served at /openapi.json
- `validation`  a zod-shaped vocabulary; a handler takes Valid<T> or does not compile
- `resource`  typed CRUD routes over one table, with the policy in the WHERE clause
- `admin`  a Django-shaped backoffice at /admin, locked until you say who may in
- `admin-model`  the admin's rows over SeaORM, one line per entity
- `realtime`  one write is a map lookup, not a query per subscriber
- `realtime-sse`  one long response per subscriber, frames written as they are made
- `commands`  this project's own command line, `serve` plus whatever you add
- `rsx`  `.rsx` templates compiled into the binary; without it a page builds a String
- `jt`  `.jt` templates compiled into the binary; a JSON answer without a struct per shape
- `rsx-tailwind`  a CSS build over the class names in your templates; needs node
- `rsx-htmx`  a click swaps what changed; the server renders from the shared layout down
- `robots`  a robots.txt from your settings, served at /robots.txt; closed outside production
- `docker`  a cargo-chef Dockerfile: slim Debian, a user that is not root, a HEALTHCHECK on /up
- `docker-kubernetes`  deploy/kubernetes.yaml: a Deployment and a Service whose probes and grace period match the drain
- `ci`  fmt, clippy and the tests on every push; pick the provider below
- `ci-github`  .github/workflows/ci.yml: fmt, clippy, tests, a Postgres service when there is a database, the image

**Absent:** `logging`, `beacon`, `static` — not compiled, not linked, absent from `Cargo.lock`. Do not write code that uses them; add the dependency and name the plugin in `main` first.

That is the framework's central rule: a capability nobody asked for is
not compiled and not linked. If you need one, add it to `Cargo.toml`
*and* name its plugin in `src/main.rs`. Nothing registers itself.

## Adding a route

A route is a file. `src/pages/about.rs` is `/about`;
`src/pages/users/[id].rs` is `/users/{id}`. **Write the file. That is
the whole of it** -- no `mod` line, no row to register, because there is
no list. `brocanth_pages::pages!` in `src/pages/mod.rs` reads this
directory while the crate compiles and writes both.

The verb comes off the handler's name: `handle` is GET, then
`handle_head`, `handle_post`, `handle_put`, `handle_patch`,
`handle_delete`, `handle_options`. A `pub fn handle_*` outside that
list is a build error naming the list, rather than a handler nothing
reaches; a page with no handler is a build error too. A private
`fn handle_*` is a helper and is left alone.

A handler may be `pub async fn` when it waits on something, such as a
database: the table awaits it and the wait holds no thread. A page that
waits on nothing stays a plain `fn`. An async handler is dropped at an
`.await` when the client goes away, so do not leave a write half done
across one.

**Adding a file does not rebuild on its own** -- nothing referenced it
yet. Run `touch src/pages/mod.rs` after creating a page or a layout.
Editing or deleting one is noticed.

A handler returns a value and never writes a response itself. That is
what makes a half-written body on an error impossible rather than
unlikely.

## Views

The markup for a route is a `.rsx` file **next to the page that renders it**:
`src/pages/index.rsx` beside `src/pages/index.rs`. There is no second tree and
nothing to register -- `rsx::load_dir!("src/pages")` in `src/pages/mod.rs`
compiles them all into the binary. One file is one module, under `views`, so
`index.rsx` is `views::index` and `users/[id].rsx` is `views::users::_id_`.

### Layouts

`layout.rsx` wraps every page in its directory **and every directory below**,
and a page never names it: which layout wraps a page is a property of where
the page is. That is the Crystal page_router's rule for `layout.cr`.

They stack root to leaf, and **the chain is not written down anywhere**.
`html!` is a macro: it knows which file it was written in, walks up to
`src/`, and wraps the page in every `layout.rsx` it passes. So
`src/pages/users/layout.rsx` wraps the pages under `users/` inside the root
layout, and deleting that file removes exactly that layer with no other edit.

Every page uses the same import and the same call, whatever directory it is
in. Do not add a chain of your own; if a page is wrapped wrongly, the
directory tree is what to change.

A layout takes `children: Element`, and may also take `layout: &str`, which
`html!` fills with the URL prefix that layout covers. Those two are the only
parameters it fills, because it cannot know what a third one would mean.
A value every page shares comes from a `const` -- the root layout reads
`pages::TITLE` that way. A value belonging to one request belongs on the page
component, which the handler builds and which already has the context.

For a fragment that is not a document -- an htmx swap, a partial -- call
`render` instead of `html!`: the same thing with no shell.

**Adding a `layout.rsx` where there was none does not rebuild anything**,
because nothing referenced the file yet. Run `touch src/pages/mod.rs` after
creating one. Editing or deleting an existing layout is noticed.

A component is a function returning `Element`. Its parameters are its contract
with the handler, and a caller fills them as struct fields, so a field the
component does not declare is a compile error rather than a blank in the page.
A parameter of type `Element` receives children, which is all a layout is.

Reach a template from a handler with `html!`, and with nothing else:

```rust
pub fn handle(_ctx: &mut Ctx) -> Result<impl IntoResponse, Error> {
    html!(ctx, views::index::Index { title: TITLE })
}
```

It returns the handler's own `Result`, so there is no `Ok(..)` to write and a
template that bails propagates with `?`. For another status or a header,
compose with the other return shapes: `Ok((html!(ctx, tpl)?, 404))`.

Adding a page with markup is two files in one directory -- `<name>.rs` and
`<name>.rsx` -- and nothing else anywhere. Neither needs a line in
`src/pages/mod.rs`, because the directory is the registry.

Not every response is a page. A redirect is `Response::empty(303)` with a
header and no template anywhere near it.

An interpolated value is escaped on the way out. Templates are read at
**compile** time, so an edit needs a rebuild, and a template that does not
parse is a build failure on its own line rather than a 500.

## Static files

Two directories, and the difference matters. `assets/` is **fingerprinted**:
`site.css` is published at `/css/site.<hash>.css` and cached for a year.
`public/` is served **verbatim**, for names that cannot move -- `robots.txt`,
`favicon.ico`, anything linked to from outside.

Never write either URL by hand. `crate::assets::url("css/site.css")` takes the
logical path and returns the published one, and a name nothing publishes
panics there rather than 404ing in a browser.

A basename starting with `_` is an input and is never published, which is what
`assets/css/_tailwind.css` is.

Both directories are embedded in the binary. **Adding a file where there was
none does not rebuild anything**; run `touch src/assets.rs` after creating one.

## Partial navigation

Link to a route with the `Link` component, never a bare `<a>`:

```
<Link to={&crate::pages::routes::users::id::path(7)}>User 7</Link>
```

`to` takes what a route helper returns, so a link to a route that does not
exist is a compile error. It renders a real `<a href>` with `dp-boost` on it,
so the page still works with no JavaScript.

A layout marks what a swap may replace with `dp-layout={layout}`, on the
element wrapping **exactly** the children. Anything inside that element is
replaced with them, so a sidebar or a scroll position belongs outside it.

A request carrying `DP-Partial: n` drops the outermost `n` layouts, and
`html!` resolves that into a `match` over the chain. A handler never reads the
header and never changes for it.

## Tasks

A command is a `clap::Args` struct with `#[cmd]` on it, in its own file under
`src/commands/`, plus a `pub mod` line at the end of `src/commands/mod.rs`,
below the line that starts `// Your commands`. `brocanth add` rewrites the
lines above it and keeps yours. The command becomes a subcommand
automatically — registration happens at link time.

```
brocanth --help      # lists this project's commands too
brocanth serve
brocanth css         # the CSS build; -W rebuilds on each change
```

The stylesheet is embedded, so a new one is a new binary. `css` rewrites
`src/assets.rs` to say so, which is what makes cargo notice.

## Decisions that belong to the person

The modules in this project are the person's choice. Do not add or
remove one on your own. Before you run `brocanth add`, show the person
the question: `brocanth add --questions` lists each module with its
default, what it needs and what it recommends. Give your
recommendation, and wait for the answer.

## House style

- A comment says **why**, next to the decision, and what was chosen
  against. Not what the line does.
- A test name is a sentence describing the guarantee it protects.
- Prefer a type that cannot be built wrong over a check that can be
  forgotten.
- State a limit where someone would look for it rather than leaving it
  to be discovered.

## Framework reference

`docs/llm-authoring.md` in the brocanth checkout is the full brief: what
cannot compile and can therefore be relied on, what can still go wrong
and therefore needs a test, and the crate map.

## Reading a body

A handler never parses `ctx.body` itself. It declares a struct with
`#[derive(zod::Entry)]`, puts the rules on the fields, and calls
`ctx.body_as()` or `ctx.read()`. The rules are values: a `const`
shared by two structs is one rule, and `zod::accepts!` makes the
compiler check a literal against it.

Report every fault, never the first. `Faults` already holds them all
and `by_name()` groups them per field; a handler that returns after
the first one makes a person submit the form three times.

Do not write `?` on a `zod::Faults`. The blanket `From` on `Error`
turns any `std::error::Error` into a 500, and a bad body is a 422.
`body_as` is the call that gets the status right.

## Edge middleware

`src/plugins/mod.rs` holds five commented registrations from
`brocanth-middleware`. Each encodes a fact about the deployment --
which proxy to trust, which host is canonical, which origins may call
-- so each is turned on by somebody who knows that fact. Do not
enable them as a set, and do not invent an address or an origin to
make one compile. To turn one on, copy it to `build()` in
`src/app.rs` and widen `type Core` by its hook families; the comment
above the five shows the type.

## Google Analytics

`brocanth_gtag::Gtag` is registered in `src/plugins/mod.rs`.
Its hook puts a consent banner and Google's tag into every HTML page,
before `</body>`. Nothing reaches Google before the visitor accepts.

Do not add a second Google tag, and do not send a page view yourself:
the hook scrubs the URL first. Never put an email address, a name or a
user id in a URL, a page title or an event: Google's terms forbid it,
and the scrubber only catches what it can recognise. A link with
`data-consent-manage` reopens the banner.

The choice lives in the visitor's browser. To keep a record of it on
the server, set `consent_log` to a file: each choice is one JSON line
with no address and no user agent.

## The admin

`src/plugins/admin/mod.rs` mounts the backoffice at `/admin`. It ships
locked: the policy is `DenyAll` and `principal` returns an anonymous
principal, so every screen answers 403. Do not open it with
`AllowAllUnsafeForDevelopment` outside a test.

A model reaches the admin through `AdminConfig::resource(..)`: a
`brocanth_admin::AdminResource` with a `brocanth_policy::Policy` over
the model's rows. A model with no resource answers 403. Never filter
rows after a read; the row policy goes into the query.

## Realtime over server-sent events

`GET /realtime/events?topics=posts/*,posts/42` streams the broker's frames
to a browser. `src/plugins/realtime_sse/mod.rs` is the stream;
`src/pages/realtime/events.rs` is the route.

- Authorise every topic in `authorise` in `src/pages/realtime/events.rs`.
  Nothing is public until it is listed in `PUBLIC` or gated there by a
  policy (`Subscription::from_policy`). Never filter frames after delivery.
- Publish from a page after the write, with the row you already hold:

  ```rust
  let realtime = ctx.provided::<Broadcast, _>().expect("a dispatched request");
  let row = brocanth_realtime::Row::new().with("author_id", author);
  realtime.broker.publish_with_row(&brocanth_events::RowChange::created("posts", id), &row);
  ```

- Read it in the browser. The event name is the topic. `lagged` means the
  view may be stale: fetch it again.

  ```js
  const events = new EventSource("/realtime/events?topics=posts/*");
  events.addEventListener("posts/*", (e) => console.log(e.data));
  events.addEventListener("lagged", () => location.reload());
  ```

## The database

`src/plugins/db/mod.rs` opens one Postgres pool at startup from `[db] url`.
A page reads it with `ctx.db()`, a `&brocanth_db::Db`. Build a statement
with `brocanth_db::sea_query`. Do not format values into SQL text: sea-query
sends each value as a bound parameter.

```rust
use brocanth_db::sea_query::{Expr, ExprTrait, Order, Query};
use brocanth_db::Exec;

use crate::pages::{Ctx, Error, IntoResponse};

pub async fn handle(ctx: &mut Ctx) -> Result<impl IntoResponse, Error> {
    let q = Query::select()
        .columns(["id", "title"])
        .from("posts")
        .and_where(Expr::col("published").eq(true))
        .order_by("id", Order::Desc)
        .limit(10)
        .to_owned();
    let posts: Vec<(i64, String)> = ctx.db().all(&q).await?;
    Ok(posts
        .iter()
        .map(|(id, title)| format!("{id} {title}\n"))
        .collect::<String>())
}
```

`ctx.db().json(&q).await?` returns each row as a `serde_json::Value`,
encoded by Postgres. Writes that belong together go in one transaction.
`Ok` commits, and `Err` rolls back:

```rust
ctx.db()
    .transact(async |tx| {
        tx.execute(&debit).await?;
        tx.execute(&credit).await?;
        Ok(())
    })
    .await?;
```

A `brocanth_db::DbError` goes through `?` as a 500. Its message goes to the
log, never to the client.

## The client

`src/commands/api.rs` is a command line for this application's own
API. It is built from `crate::pages::described()` at run time, not
generated, so there is nothing to regenerate and nothing to keep in
step: add a page with a typed signature and the client grows a
subcommand with the right flags.

Do not add validation to it. The server checks the body and answers
422 with every fault; a client that checked as well would be a second
opinion, and the two would disagree the first time a rule changed.

## CSRF

`brocanth_middleware::Csrf` is registered in `src/plugins/mod.rs`. It
is a double-submit cookie: the hook mints a token, sets it as its own
cookie, and refuses any verb that is not GET, HEAD, OPTIONS or TRACE
unless the request sends the same value back -- in the `_csrf_token`
field, or in the `X-CSRF-Token` header.

So every form that posts carries the hidden field. In a page, read
the token with `ctx.hooked::<brocanth_middleware::CsrfToken>()` and
write `token.hidden_field()` inside the `<form>`. For HTML this
project did not template, `token.stamp_forms(html)` adds the field to
every posting form; the admin uses it.

A 403 from this hook is a form that lost its token, or a caller that
is not a browser. Add that path to `exempt`; do not remove the
registration.

## Analytics

`brocanth_analytics::Analytics` is registered in `src/plugins/mod.rs`.
It counts every GET answered with `text/html`, except paths under
`[analytics] exclude`, bots and prefetches. Nothing to add to a page:
no script, no cookie, no banner.

Do not put personal data in a URL. The path and the allowed query
parameters are stored; an email-shaped segment is replaced, but a name
or an account number is not. Do not add a column to
`brocanth_analytics_views` that identifies a person.

With the admin, the numbers are at `/admin/analytics`, behind the
admin's policy like every tab.

## Security headers

`brocanth_middleware::SecurityHeaders` is registered in
`src/plugins/mod.rs`. Its Content-Security-Policy
allows inline scripts by hash only. To inline a new script, add
`Csp::default().inline_script(TEXT)` with the exact text between the
tags. Do not add `'unsafe-inline'` to `script-src`. A value that
depends on the request goes in a `data-` attribute or a `<meta>` tag,
not in the script.

HSTS is sent only over HTTPS. Set `behind_tls` when a TLS terminator
is in front. Set `include_subdomains` or `preload` only when the
person who owns the domain says so.

## Rate limit

`brocanth_middleware::RateLimit` is registered in
`src/plugins/mod.rs` with one example rule (`login`, 5 per 60 s).
The numbers are an example. Do not invent limits: ask for the limit
and the window of each route group.

A request whose key cannot be found is not counted. Behind a proxy,
the address comes from `ProxyHeaders` or from `ip_header`. Never set
`ip_header` to a header the client can send, such as
`X-Forwarded-For`, unless the edge overwrites it.
